THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 6, 1935

General Sung Cheh-yuan
Causes Flurry By Sudden
Departure For Tientsin

Written Statement Interpreted In Chinese Circles
To Indicate That He Will No Longer Assume
Full Responsibility For Peiping

GENERAL HO YING-CHIN CONFERS WITH
LEADING MILITARY COMMANDERS

PEIPING; Dec. 5.—A flurry was caused in local Chinese circles to-day by the sudden, unexpected departure from the ancient capital of General Sung Cheh-yuan, Garrison Commander of Peiping and Tientsin, whose exit cast a damper on the optimism prevailing here that the crisis in North China would soon be composed.

General Sung was at first reported to have gone to a villa in the Western Hills, near Peiping, but this appears to have been a blind, for it was reliably reported this evening that he had arrived at Tientsin. General Sung, who has a house in the British Concession there, is stated to have made the journey by road and to have arrived at his destination this afternoon.

A written statement issued this afternoon by General Sung is interpreted in Chinese circles as indicating that he will no longer assume full responsibility for the maintenance of peace and order in Peiping.

Confidence In Ho

The statement declares that the situation in North China has greatly improved since the arrival of General Ho, and that he is confident that the Chinese War Minister will be able to find a solution.

General Sung refers to his task, as commandant of the Peiping and Tientsin garrisons, of maintaining peace and order, and adds:

"Now that General Ho Ying-chin has come to Peiping, I feel that my work has been considerably lightened. Henceforth, I will deal with all difficult problems in accordance with instructions from General Ho."

The craft circled above the "Chü Jen-tang" hall, the temporary residence of General Ho Yin-chin, Chinese Minister of War, who arrived here on Tuesday empowered by the Nanking Government to take whatever measures he should find necessary to settle the North China situation.—Rengo.

Palace Museum Treasures

PEIPING, Dec. 3.—According to Chinese reports, the Palace Museum is sending shortly 500 cases of art treasures to Nanking and Shanghai.

The decision to ship the treasures from Peiping was made after the return of Mr. Chang Ting-chi, Director of the Department of General of the Museum, from Shanghai last week.

The Curio Museum is also arranging to remove its art treasures to Nanking. This Museum is under the control of the Ministry of the Interior in Nanking, while the Palace Museum is under the Executive Yuan direct.—Reuter.

PEIPING, Dec. 5.—"I am well and safe," declared Mr. Yin Ju-keng, head of the so-called Autonomous State of East Hopei, when told of a report widely circulated in China yesterday that he had been assassinated.

Mr. Yin readily came to the telephone when inquirers rang up his headquarters at Tungchow, in the Demilitarized Zone, from Peiping.

He added that all was quiet in Tungchow, and that he was proceeding steadily with his arrangements for the administration of the new "State."—Reuter.

Aerial Demonstrations

PEIPING, Dec. 5.—The Japanese are subjecting Peiping to thorough aerial demonstrations. Aeroplanes circled over the headquarters of General Ho Yin-chin yesterday, while to-day 14 Japanese machines, as well as a plane belonging to the so-called Autonomous Government of East Hopei, visited the ancient capital.

The "East Hopei," a plane which formerly belonged to the Japanese and which was piloted by a Japanese, flew over the city at one o'clock this afternoon, dropping thousands of leaflets which called for support of the "autonomous scheme" and offered congratulations to the East Hopei Council on their inauguration.

Then, at 2.30 p.m., five planes flying in formation roared low over the city, being followed an hour later by nine planes, which also flew in formation.

The planes were obviously not reconnoitring, but were purely for purposes of demonstration. Their origin is unknown, but as they came out from the North, it is probable that they were from Jehol.

Tsao Kun In Tientsin

TIENTSIN, Dec. 5.—Contrary to current reports, General Tsao Kun, former leader of the Chihli clique, has not gone to Peiping, but is still in Tientsin, confining himself to his residence in the British Concession here and amusing himself with Chinese painting. Except with General Wu Pei-fu, with whom he is in frequent communication, it is understood that General Tsao has refused to receive all his other former followers.—Chekiai.

Refugees In Tangshan

TIENTSIN, Dec. 5.—In view of the troublous situation in the East Hopei following the establishment of the so-called Autonomous Government by Yin Ju-keng, most of the well-to-do inhabitants there have left their homes to seek refuge in Tangshan. Owing to the sudden increase of population, it is learned that all the vacant unoccupied houses in Tangshan have been filled to overflowing.—Chekiai.

A Chinese Report

LONDON, Dec. 5.—Disturbances among Hopei peasants following the autonomous movement in the province were reported here today. It is said that many villages have been looted by the bandits operating in the area.

《字林西报》，1935年12月6日，星期五

宋哲元将军
因突然启程前往天津
引起一阵骚动

中文界人士解读其书面声明
意指他将不再承担北平的全部责任

何应钦将军与主要军事指挥官会谈

北平，12月5日电。——北平及天津卫戍司令宋哲元将军今日突然且出人意料地离开这座古都，在当地华人圈子中引起了一阵骚动，他的离去给此处普遍存在的、认为华北危机即将平息的那种乐观情绪泼了一盆冷水。

起初有报道称宋将军已前往北平附近的西山别墅，但这似乎是个障眼法，因为今晚有可靠消息指出，他已抵达天津。据悉，宋将军在天津英租界有一处住宅，他是经由陆路旅行，并于今天下午抵达目的地。

宋将军今天下午发表的一份书面声明，被中文界人士解读为表明他将不再承担维持北平治安秩序的全部责任。

对何的信任

该声明宣称，自何将军抵达以来，华北局势已大为改善，并且他相信中国军政部长能够找到解决方案。

宋将军提及他作为北平及天津卫戍司令维持治安秩序的任务，并补充道：

“既然何应钦将军已来到北平，我觉得我的工作已大大减轻。此后，我将根据何将军的指示处理所有棘手问题。”

一架飞机在中国军政部长何应钦将军的临时寓所“居仁堂”上空盘旋，何将军于周二抵达此处，获南京政府授权采取其认为必要的任何措施以解决华北局势。——联合通讯社。

故宫博物院珍宝

北平，12月3日电。——据中文报道，故宫博物院不久将把500箱艺术珍宝运往南京和上海。

将珍宝从北平运出的决定，是在博物院总务处处长张廷济先生上周从上海返回后作出的。

古物陈列所也在安排将其艺术珍宝迁往南京。该陈列所受南京内政部管辖，而故宫博物院则直隶行政院。——路透社。

北平，12月5日电。——“我安好无恙，”所谓冀东自治国首领殷汝耕先生在被告知昨日在中国广泛流传的他已被暗杀的报道时宣称。

当询问者从北平打电话到他在非武装区通县的总部时，殷先生 readily 接听了电话。

他补充说，通县一切平静，他正稳步进行新“国家”行政管理的安排工作。——路透社。

空中示威

北平，12月5日电。——日本人正对北平进行彻底的空中示威。昨天，飞机在中国军政部长何应钦将军的总部上空盘旋，而今天，14架日本飞机以及一架属于所谓冀东自治政府的飞机造访了这座古都。

“冀东号”是一架前属日本所有、由一名日本人驾驶的飞机，于今天下午一点钟飞越该市，投下数千份传单，呼吁支持“自治方案”，并向冀东委员会的就职表示祝贺。

随后，在下午2点30分，五架编队飞行的飞机在城市上空低空呼啸而过，一小时后又有九架同样编队飞行的飞机紧随其后。

这些飞机显然不是在侦察，而纯粹是为了示威目的。它们的来源不明，但由于它们从北方飞来，很可能来自热河。

曹锟在天津

天津，12月5日电。——与当前传闻相反，直系前首领曹锟将军并未前往北平，仍留在天津，闭门居于其在本地英租界的寓所中，以中国画自娱。据了解，除了与他保持频繁联络的吴佩孚将军外，曹将军已拒绝接见所有其他 former 追随者。——浙报。

唐山难民

天津，12月5日电。——鉴于殷汝耕建立所谓自治政府后冀东局势动荡，当地大多数富裕居民已离家前往唐山避难。据悉，由于人口突然增加，唐山所有空置无人居住的房屋均已人满为患。——浙报。

一则中文报道

伦敦，12月5日电。——今日在此报道了河北省自治运动之后河北农民发生的骚乱。据说许多村庄遭到在该地区活动的匪徒洗劫。

Newspapers' Bitter Comment
TIENTSIN, Dec. 5.—Coincident-
ally with an apparent hardening
of the attitude of Chinese leaders
in the North on the autonomy
question, the Japanese newspapers
here to-day assume a bitterly
hostile tone towards the latest
developments in North China.
Both General Sung Cheh-yuan,
Garrison Commander of Peiping
and Tientsin, who yesterday an-
nounced his continued loyalty to
Nanking and determination to
resist external pressure, and
General Ho Ying-chin, Chinese
War Minister, are vigorously
criticized.
The Japanese press affects to see
in General Ho's return to North
China the prospect of an early re-
newal of anti-Japanese activities
by organizations like the "Blue
Shirts."
Educational leaders here to-day
sent a telegram to General Ho
Ying-chin and Hopei military lead-
ers proclaiming unanimous opposi-
tion to the autonomy movement,
and promising full support for a
settlement safe-guarding the sov-
ereignty and integrity of China.—
Reuter.

Nanking Daily Protests
NANKING, Dec. 5. — The
"Central Daily News," in a leader
to-day, vigorously protests against
the ban imposed by the Tientsin
and Peiping authorities on the "Ta
Kung Pao," well-known Tientsin
Chinese paper.
The leader expresses surprise
that the action taken against the
"Ta Kung Pao" was the result of
an editorial urging the Northern
authorities to maintain China's
territorial integrity, and indignant-
ly asks:
"Are Peiping and Tientsin still
Chinese territory? Do the
authorities there consider them-
selves Chinese officials?"
The journal then draws a con-
trast between the ban on the "Ta
Kung Pao" and the distribution of
autonomist propaganda in Peiping
and Tientsin, and demands an ex-
planation from the authorities
there concerning "their surprising
course of action."
In conclusion, the "Central Daily
News" pays a tribute to the press
and intelligentsia in North China
for their strong opposition to the
autonomist movement, and urges
newspapers throughout the country
to carry on with their duties to-
wards the public "with the zeal of
religious martyrs."
The "Ta Kung Pao," which is
known throughout China as a fear-
less and outspoken organ of Chin-
ese public opinion, was banned
from Peiping on December 4.
It may be recalled that the
vigorour stand made recently by
the "Central Daily News" for
liberalization of the censorship
regulations won hearty nationwide
response.

"Ta Kung Pao" Ban Lifted
NANKING, Dec. 5.--The Min-
istry of Communications to-day
announced the Tientsin Post
Office stating that the ban on
the transmission of the "Ta Kung
Pao" through the mails is lifted.
The ban had been imposed by
the local authorities because the
"Ta Kung Pao"—one of the lead-
ing newspapers in China—had
urged the Northern authorities to
maintain China's territorial in-
tegrity.—Reuter.

报纸的严厉评论

天津，12月5日电。——与此同时，随着北方中国领导人在自治问题上态度明显强硬，这里的日本报纸今天对华北的最新事态发展采取了极其敌对的语调。无论是昨天宣布继续效忠南京并决心抵抗外部压力的北平及天津卫戍司令宋哲元将军，还是中国军政部长何应钦将军，都受到了猛烈批评。

日本报界装作在何将军返回华北一事中看到了诸如“蓝衣社”等组织早日重启反日活动的迹象。

这里的教育界领袖今天向何应钦将军及河北军事领导人发出电报，宣布一致反对自治运动，并承诺全力支持达成一项保障中国主权和领土完整的解决方案。——路透社。

《中央日报》抗议

南京，12月5日电。——《中央日报》在今日的一篇社论中，强烈抗议天津和北平当局对知名天津中文报纸《大公报》实施的禁令。

该社论对针对《大公报》采取的行动竟是源于一篇敦促北方当局维护中国领土完整的社论表示惊讶，并愤慨地问道：

“北平和天津还是中国领土吗？那里的当局还认为自己是中国的官员吗？”

该报随后将禁止《大公报》与在北平和天津分发自治主义宣传品进行对比，并要求当地当局就其“令人惊讶的行径”作出解释。

最后，《中央日报》赞扬华北新闻界和知识界强烈反对自治运动，并敦促全国各地的报纸“以宗教殉道者般的热忱”履行其对公众的职责。

《大公报》作为中国舆论界无畏且直言不讳的喉舌闻名全国，于12月4日在北平被禁。

值得回顾的是，《中央日报》最近为放宽审查制度所采取的坚定立场赢得了全国范围内的热烈响应。

解除对《大公报》的禁令

南京，12月5日电。——交通部今天宣布，天津邮局表示，解除通过邮件传递《大公报》的禁令。

该禁令是由地方当局实施的，原因是《大公报》——中国主要报纸之一——曾敦促北方当局维护中国的领土完整。——路透社。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 3. 1935
S. L. REGISTER
D. 1935 / 108
5

IMPARTIAL NOT NEUTRAL

A RÉSUMÉ

Events in North China find their origin in the absorption of Jehol by Manchoukuo with the support of Japanese troops early in 1934 and the subsequent signature of the Tangku Truce on May 31, of that year. That agreement created the demilitarized zone—an area of 5,000 square miles between the Great Wall and a line running from Yenching to Lutai. It was accompanied by certain verbal undertakings given by the Chinese signatories to the Japanese. On the basis of those undisclosed terms negotiations between the Japanese military authorities and the Chinese administration in the North have, from time to time, been conducted. The tenor of each pronouncement on such negotiations has established the fact that a wide freedom of interpretation has been consistently reserved by the Japanese, so that in handling affairs in the North the Chinese authorities have been compelled to follow Japanese dictation which has developed an appetite by the mere process of feeding. On May of this year this journal's Peiping correspondent reported a sudden turn in the course of events in the presentation to General Ho Ying-chin, the Chairman of the Peiping Military Council (and War Minister in the National Government) of certain demands from the Kwantung Army. These demands were indicated by the subsequent removal of the headquarters of the Hopei Provincial Government from Tientsin to Paotingfu, the elimination from the Peiping Military Council of elements declared to be unsatisfactory to the Japanese, the closing of the local Kuomintang offices, and the withdrawal—carried out with lightning speed—of General Yu Hsueh-chang's troops and the resignation of the General himself from the charge of the Hopei Government. The activities of Sun Yung-chin at the head of so-called Chinese volunteers in the demilitarized zone and the murder of two Japanophile Chinese editors in the Japanese Concession in Tientsin were the ostensible causes of this action by the Kwantung Army. Early in June the removal of General Sung Cheh-yuan from the Governorship of Charhar, together with all his troops, was also demanded. General Ho Ying-chin was pressed to give a written acceptance of the Japanese demands but he declined and reported to the Government at Nanking on June 12.

On June 18 it was announced that the Government had replaced General Sung Cheh-yuan in the Governorship of Charhar by General Chin Teh-chung and had appointed Mr. Wang Keh-min to be acting Chairman of the Peiping Military Council in place of General Huang Fu who had held that appointment since May 1934 and had retired owing to ill-health. Meanwhile the Kwantung Army announced that General Sung Cheh-yuan and his troops, having broken the Tangku Truce would be regarded as bandits. On June 27, Major-General Kenji Doihara secured the written agreement of General Chin Teh-chung to a settlement of the Charhar dispute, including reparation for the arrest of four civilian employees of the Kwantung Army at Changpei on June 5. Rumours of a separatist movement were current and on June 28 some insurgents—among whom were Japanese "ronin" subsequently deported to Japan—seized an armoured train and with it launched an attack on Peiping. The attempt was quickly suppressed by the local Chinese authorities. A lull in the situation then followed until on August 4 the murder of Colonel Liu Tso-chiu of the Peace Preservation Corps and the wounding of Japanese gendarme by Chinese assailants prompted an urgent representation by the Japanese military authorities to Mr. Wang Keh-min, the conversation including a suggestion that the five northern provinces should be reorganized. Mr. Tao Shang-min, an inspector of the demilitarized zone was detained at the Japanese Embassy on August 6 and not released until August 17. after a protest by the Government at Nanking. On August 28, General

Sung Cheh-Yuan, having apparently lost his "bandit" status on the Japanese books, was appointed Garrison Commander of the Peiping-Tientsin area with enhanced powers. The Government also decided on the same day to abolish the Peiping Political Council — a decision which took effect on September 1, thus terminating the two years' existence of a sorely-tried organization. On September 2 to General Shang Chen who, as persona grata to the Japanese, had been appointed to succeed General Yu Hsueh-chang as Chairman of the Hopei Government in June, the Japanese Consul-General at Tientsin reiterated the demand for the suppression of terrorist organizations in Hopei and accused the provincial authorities of negligence in that regard. On September 25 disclosure of a Japanese military memorandum —attributed to the staff of General Tada—outlined a definite scheme of autonomy for the Northern provinces of China. Political and economic collaboration between China, Japan and Manchoukuo was commended by an official announcement at Tokyo toward the end of September. On October 18, Mr. Akira Ariyoshi in an interview with this journal referred to the situation in the North as "not unsatisfactory," but affirmed Japan's policy of regarding the Government at Nanking as the Central Government of China. 《字林西报》，1935年12月3日，星期二
S. L. 登记册
D. 1935 / 108
5

公正而非中立

摘要

华北事端的起源，在于1934年初在日本军队支持下热河被满洲国吞并，以及同年5月31日随后签署的《塘沽停战协定》。该协定划定了非军事区——即长城与从燕京至芦台一线之间的一片5,000平方英里的区域。伴随该协定的是中方签署方向日方作出的某些口头承诺。基于这些未公开的条款，日本军方当局与中国北方行政当局之间的谈判不时进行。每次关于此类谈判的声明基调都确立了一个事实，即日方始终保留广泛的解释自由，致使中国当局在处理北方事务时被迫听从日方的指令，而日方的胃口仅通过这种喂饲过程便日益膨胀。今年5月，本报北平记者报道，关东军向北平军分会委员长（兼国民政府军政部长）何应钦将军提出某些要求后，事态发展出现突变。这些要求体现在随后河北省政府总部从天津迁往保定府、北平军分会中被日方认为不满的人员被清除、当地国民党办事处被关闭，以及于学忠将军部队迅速撤离及其本人辞去河北省政府职务之中。孙永勤在非军事区率领所谓“义勇军”的活动，以及在天津日租界两名亲日华籍编辑被杀，是关东军采取此次行动的借口。6月初，日方还要求撤换察哈尔省主席宋哲元将军及其全部部队。日方向何应钦将军施压，要求其书面接受日方要求，但何予以拒绝，并于6月12日向南京政府报告。

6月18日宣布，政府任命秦德纯将军接替宋哲元将军担任察哈尔省主席，并任命王克敏先生代理北平军分会委员长，以取代自1934年5月起担任该职因病退休的黄郛将军。与此同时，关东军宣布，宋哲元将军及其部队违反《塘沽停战协定》，将被视为匪徒。6月27日，土肥原贤二少将取得了秦德纯将军关于解决察哈尔争端的书面协议，其中包括就6月5日在张北逮捕四名关东军平民雇员一事进行赔偿。分离运动的谣言流传，6月28日，一些叛乱分子——其中包括随后被驱逐至日本的日本“浪人”——劫持了一列装甲列车，并借此发动对北平的进攻。该企图被中国地方当局迅速镇压。随后局势出现短暂平静，直到8月4日，保安总队刘佐舟上校被杀及一名日本宪兵被中国袭击者打伤，促使日本军方当局向王克敏先生提出紧急交涉，谈话中包括改组华北五省的建议。非军事区督察陶尚民先生于8月6日被拘押在日本大使馆，直至8月17日经南京政府抗议后才获释。8月28日，宋

哲元将军显然已不再被日方列为“匪徒”，被任命为平津卫戍司令，权力扩大。政府同日决定撤销北平政务委员会——该决定于9月1日生效，从而终结了这个饱受磨难的组织两年的存在。9月2日，驻天津日本总领事向商震将军重申了镇压河北恐怖组织的要求，并指责省政府在此方面疏忽大意；商震将军因受日方青睐，曾于6月被任命接替于学忠将军担任河北省政府主席。9月25日，一份据称出自多田将军参谋部的日本军事备忘录披露，概述了中国北方各省自治的具体方案。9月底，东京官方公告赞扬中、日、满之间的政治与经济合作。10月18日，有吉明在接受本报采访时称华北局势“并非令人不满”，但重申日本视南京政府为中国中央政府的政策。日本外交与军事

in Shanghai two days later. Mr.
Ariyoshi's interpretation was con-
firmed by Major-General Y.
Okamura, who attended the con-
ference as a special representative
of the Japanese General Staff.
On October 22 more trouble oc-
curred in the demilitarized zone as
the result of the dissatisfaction of
farmers with certain new taxes.
The outbreak was taken as the text
for Japanese criticism of General
Shang Chen's administration. The
revolt was suppressed and General
Tada was reported to have agreed
to deal with certain Japanese
"ronin" who had participated in it.
On October 30 a formal warning to
General Shang Chen, General Sung
Cheh-yuan and the mayors of Pei-
ping and Tientsin, was given by
the Japanese Consul-General and on
the next day the Kwantung Army
authorities followed it up by de-
manding a suppression of all anti-
Japanese activities. On November
15 the concentration of Japanese
troops in Shanhaikuan aroused
new apprehensions. Three days
later General Hsiao Chen-ying who
had succeeded General Chin
Teh-chung as Governor of Charhar
revealed the intention immediately
to create an autonomous North-
ern China. This revelation was
quickly followed by a reported
statement from General Doihara to
the effect that the Kwantung Army
was prepared to support an
autonomous movement. It seemed
that the plan for separation was
ripe, but in spite of Japanese pres-
sure on the leading figures in the
North, no definite break occurred
and the provincial authorities
maintained touch with the Govern-
ment at Nanking where the National
Congress of the Kuomintang was
concluding its Fifth Session. Mr.
Ariyoshi visited Nanking to discuss
the affairs of the North with General
Chiang Kai-shek and, apparently,
General Doihara's move had been
checked. It was suggested, however,
that the Kwantung Army would not
accept the rebuff and on November
22 the Japanese military spokesman
at Tientsin significantly declared
that the "current toward autonomy
was still flowing." On November 24,
Mr. Yin Ju-keng, an administrative
inspector of the demilitarized zone
with Japanese affiliations, proclaimed
the autonomy of twenty-five hsien of
Eastern Hopei. The next day General
Doihara reappeared in Peiping. On
November 27 Japanese troops oc-
cupied Fengtai railway junction,
commandeered wagons, and took
charge of the Chinese military tele-
phone service. On November 29 the
Chinese Government formally pro-
tested against this seizure and
against the activities of Japanese
officers in assisting the autonomy
movement. On November 30 the
Peiping Military Council was dis-
solved by orders from Nanking
and General Ho Ying-chin was de-
puted to proceed to Peiping at once
as resident representative of the
Executive Yuan at Peiping. With
him were to be associated General
Chen I, chairman of the Fukien
Government; General Hsiung Shih-
hui, Chairman of the Kiangsi Gov-
ernment and Mr. Yin Tung formerly
of the Peiping-Mukden Railway. It
was hoped that these distinguished
officials would be able to find
a satisfactory formula for the solu-
tion of the Government's difficulties
in the North. The omens were not
favourable as will be gathered from
this brief résumé of events since the
Tangku Truce was signed and de-
livered into Japanese hands such
elastic control over North China's
occasions and destiny.

秦德纯之后担任察哈尔省主席的
萧振瀛将军透露了立即建立华北
自治的意图。这一透露很快随之
传来土肥原将军的声明，称关东
军准备支持自治运动。分裂计划
似乎已成熟，但尽管日方对北方
要员施加压力，并未发生明确的
决裂，各省当局仍与南京政府保
持联系，当时国民党第五次全国
代表大会正在南京闭幕。有吉明
访问南京，与蒋介石将军讨论华
北事务，显然，土肥原将军的举
动受到了遏制。然而，有人指出
关东军不会接受这一挫折，11月
22日，驻天津的日本军方发言人
意味深长地宣称，“自治潮流仍
在涌动”。11月24日，具有日本背
景的非军事区行政督察殷汝耕宣
布冀东二十五县自治。次日，土
肥原将军再次出现在北平。11月
27日，日军占领丰台铁路枢纽，
征用货车，并接管了中国军用电
话服务。11月29日，中国政府正
式抗议此次抢占行为以及日本军
官协助自治运动的活动。11月30
日，北平军分会奉南京命令解散，
何应钦将军被委派立即前往北平，
担任行政院驻北平办事处长官。
与他一同任事的还有福建省政府
主席陈仪将军、江西省政府主席
熊式辉将军以及前北宁铁路的殷
同先生。人们希望这些显要官员
能够为解决政府在华北的困境找
到令人满意的方案。但从《塘沽
停战协定》签署并将如此弹性的
控制权交予日方手中以来，华北
的际遇与命运所经历的这段简要
事件回顾来看，前景并不乐观。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 3, 1935
126216

PAOTING CONFERENCE
OPENS AT NIGHT

Generals Open Talks On
Future Status Of
North China

PAOTING, Dec. 2.—Political
and military leaders of North
China went into conference with
General Ho Ying-chin, Minister
of War, here to-night.
Attending the meeting, which
was held in the home of General
Shang Chen, Chairman of the
Hopei Provincial Government,
were General Hsiung Shih-hui,
Chairman of the Kiangsi Provin-
cial Government, who accompani-
ed General Ho here from Nan-
king; General Sung Cheh-yuan,
Garrison Commander of the Pei-
ping-Tientsin Area, General
Jung Chin and General Pao Wen-
yueh, members of the now defunct
Peiping Branch Military Council
and General Shang.
The conference opened at about
10 o'clock after a dinner at the
home of the Provincial Chairman
earlier in the evening.
General Hsiao Chang-ying,
Chairman of the Chahar Provin-
cial Government, who left Peiping
at 1.30 o'clock for Paotingfu de-
trained at Changhsintien, half-
way en route, and returned to the
former capital.
Soldiers with fixed bayonets
surrounded the Shang residence
on the ill-lit and narrow Hsian-
chinyu-kai, the "Street of the
Gold Fish," keeping all comers at
a distance.
The party of officials from Pei-
ping arrived here at 4.30 o'clock
together with the Rengo corres-
pondent. They were all on hand
at the station when General Ho's
trained pulled in from the South
at 8.20 o'clock.—Rengo.

B. D. 2106
5

General Ho, who was smartly
dressed, descended from the train
a few minutes after it had pulled
into the station and exchanged
greetings with the many colleagues
with whom he had worked so long
in Peiping.
With the greetings over, the
Minister of War left with General
Shang Chen for the latter's
residence where the conference is
being held.
Prior to leaving with General
Shang, the Minister of War de-
clined all interviews with the press.
—Reuter.

Reuter's Report
PAOTINGFU, Dec. 2.—The
situation in North China was dis-
cussed at an important conference
which opened here to-night be-
tween General Ho Ying-chin,
Minister of War and recently
appointed Resident Representative
of the Nanking Government, and
General Shang Chen, Governor of
Hopei.
The two leaders were still con-
ferring at a late hour to-night, but
nothing concerning their discus-
sions has been disclosed.
General Ho arrived at 8.30
p.m., but is not expected to make a
long stay here, as he left his body-
guard and staff aboard his special
train which has steam up and is
ready to leave at any time. It is
probable that the Minister of War
will leave for Peiping late to-night
or early to-morrow morning.
According to Reuter's special
correspondent, when General Ho's
special train pulled into the station
to-night, a vast concourse of
people was crowded outside the
station, while the platform was
filled with civil and military au-
thorities. Among the latter were
General Shang Chen, Generals
Wang Yung-chun and Pao Wen-yueh,
Vice-Chairmen of the new defunct
Peiping Military Council.
Many of the most important
members of the staff of the former
Military Council had travelled
around from Peiping to welcome
the Minister.

《字林西报》，1935年12月3日，星期二
126216

保定会议
夜间开幕

将领们就华北
未来地位问题
展开会谈

保定，12月2日电。——今晚，华北的政治和军事领导人在此与军政部长何应钦将军举行会议。
出席在河北省政府主席商震将军寓所举行的会议的有：陪同何将军从南京来此的江西省政府主席熊式辉将军；平津卫戍司令宋哲元将军；已解散的北平分会军事委员会成员荣臻将军、鲍文樾将军以及商将军。
会议于当晚在省主席寓所共进晚餐后，约10点钟开始。
察哈尔省政府主席萧振瀛将军于1时30分离开北平前往保定府，途中在长辛店下车，返回故都。
手持上刺刀步枪的士兵包围了位于灯光昏暗且狭窄的“金鱼胡同”（Hsianchinyu-kai）的商宅，将所有人挡在外面。
来自北平的官员一行人与联合通讯社记者于4时30分抵达此处。当何将军的专列于8时20分从南方进站时，他们均在车站等候。——联合社。

B. D. 2106
5

衣着整洁的何将军在列车进站几分钟后下车，并与许多曾在北平长期共事的同僚互致问候。
问候结束后，军政部长随商震将军前往后者寓所，会议正在那里举行。
在随商将军离开之前，军政部长拒绝了所有媒体采访。——路透社。

路透社报道
保定府，12月2日电。——今晚在此间召开的一次重要会议上，讨论了华北局势。与会者包括军政部长兼新任南京政府驻平代表何应钦将军，以及河北省主席商震将军。
两位领导人深夜仍在磋商，但关于讨论内容的任何细节均未披露。
何将军于晚上8时30分抵达，但预计不会在此久留，因为他将警卫和参谋人员留在了他的专列上，该列车已生火待发，随时可以启程。军政部长很可能在今晚深夜或明早前往北平。
据路透社特派记者称，今晚何将军的专列进站时，站外聚集了大量人群，而站台上则挤满了文武官员。后者中包括商震将军，以及新近解散的北平军事委员会副主席王以哲将军和鲍文樾将军。
前军事委员会参谋部的许多重要成员已从北平赶来欢迎部长。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 3, 1935
War Minister Arrives
In Paotingfu; Enters
Into Parleys At Once
Formation Of Northern Political Council Having
Control Over Five Provinces Discussed In
Well-Informed Circles In Peiping
JAPANESE MILITARY IMPATIENT OVER
CONTINUED UNSETTLED CONDITIONS
PEIPING, Dec. 2.—The one question being asked here
to-day is whether General Ho Ying-chin, the Chinese War
Minister, who has been sent to Peiping by the Nanking
Government as Resident Representative of the Executive
Yuan, will be able to save the five Northern Provinces, or
part of them, for China. It is felt that he has a fairly good
chance of organizing a form of semi-independent adminis-
tration which will go a long way towards meeting Japanese
requirements, while remaining nominally under the control
of Nanking. Well-informed Chinese are discussing the
possibility of the formation of a body to be known as the
Northern Political Council of the Republic of China, which
would control the provinces of Hopei, Shantung, Shansi,
Chahar and Suiyuan.
It is suggested that this Coun-
cil be a fairly large body of per-
haps 40 members, including a
number of retired Northern milit-
arists and officials residing in
this area, but that unquestionably,
General Sung Cheh-yuan, Garrison
Commander of Peiping and
Tientsin, must head the Council,
as he is the only man in this
area with sufficient troops to
maintain peace and order. The
status of the new body would be
similar to that of the Mongol
Autonomous Council.
The plan, it is believed, might
be accepted by the Japanese.
Major-General Doihara, of the
Kwantung Army, is understood
to have already discussed with
General Sung Cheh-yuan, and to
have indicated his readiness to
discuss it further. It is evident,
however, that settlement of
North China's affairs brooks of
no delays.
The Japanese military spokes-
man indicated to-day the growing
impatience of the Japanese milit-
ary authorities over the unsettled
conditions of North China.
Asked about the autonomy
movement, he said that it was
"still progressing, but no im-
mediate developments were to be
expected." If General Ho Ying-
chin came to Peiping, he added,
no negotiations would be carried
on with him, although he might
visit the Japanese authorities.
Autonomy, he added, would come
first, and then afterwards there
might be a discussion of an ad-
ministration and council for this
area.
Peiping Mayor's Wire
General Chin Teh-chun, the
Mayor of Peiping, to-day tele-
graphed to the Nanking authori-
ties urging them to devise
measures to deal with the situa-
tion in North China.
It is felt that this action by
General Chin, together with the
recent statements made by Mr.
Ching Keh, Mayor of Tientsin,
and General Sung Cheh-yuan,
pave the way for the declaration
of autonomy, while they fear they
will inevitably be forced to make.
Major-General Doihara, accord-
ing to a high Chinese official, has
intimated to General Sung that
further delay in satisfying the
situation and the autonomist
demands will be difficult.
General Sung is reported to
have replied that, as long as the
demonstrations are orderly, the
authorities will not interfere with
them.
General Sung and other officials
are going to Paotingfu, the Hopei
provincial capital, to meet Gen-
eral Ho Ying-chin, who arrives
there to-day.
It is expected that they will
confer with General Shang Chen,
Governor of Hopei, but whether
General Ho will come to Peiping
after all is doubtful in view of
his reported statement at Hsu-
chow: He is said to have express-
ed uncertainty whether he would
assume his new post at Peiping.
Questioned to-day concerning
the reported arrival at Shan-
haikwan of ten Japanese troop
trains from Mukden, the Japan-
ese military spokesmen declared
that he had no information con-
cerning the matter.
Persistent reports that three
divisions of troops are being sent
from Japan to North China are
discredited in all well-informed
quarters here.—Reuter.
Autonomy Committee
NANKING, Dec. 2.—Well-in-
formed circles here state that
General Sung Cheh-yuan, Garri-
son Commander of Peiping and
Tientsin, has suggested the est-
ablishment of a Hopei Anti-Red
Autonomy Committee with him-
self as Chairman.
It is further stated that this
suggestion will be discussed by
General Ho Ying-chin, Minister
of War, and General Sung.—
Reuter.
General Cheng Yi
TIENTSIN, Dec. 2.—General
Cheng Yi, Governor of Fukien,
who arrived here this morning
from Nanking, will leave to-night
for Peiping.
He refused to grant any inter-
views, but his departure for
Peiping is regarded as indicat-
ing that the establish-
ment of the new regime in
North China is imminent.
It is believed here that General
Ho, who is en route to Paotingfu,
will remain there until he hears
from General Cheng Yi before
leaving for Peiping.
Mr. Ching Keh, the Mayor of
Tientsin, signalized his return
from Peiping to-day by despatch-
ing a number of telegrams urging
that the Chinese Government take
the initiative in establishing an
autonomous regime in North
China in order to preserve China's
sovereign rights.
The director and representatives
of the nine autonomy districts in
Tientsin have telegraphed to Nan-
king urging the Central Govern-
ment to take effective measures
for the safety of Hopei, and de-
claring that district autonomy
was the best solution for the pres-
ent difficulties. A similar tele-
gram was despatched by the Chin-
ese Chamber of Commerce.—
Reuter.
Uncertain Whether To Assume Post
NANKING, Dec. 2.—Interview-
ed when he passed through Hsu-
chow yesterday, General Ho Ying-
chin is reported to have told
pressmen that he was uncertain
whether he would assume his new
post at Peiping.—Reuter.
Dr. Wang Calls On Hirota
TOKYO, Dec. 2.—Dr. C. T.
Wang, formerly Minister for For-
eign Affairs at Nanking, called
at the Foreign Office this morn-
ing and had an interview with Mr.
Hirota, the Japanese Minister for
Foreign Affairs, and Mr. Shige-
mitsu, the Vice-Minister.
Discussing the Sino-Japanese
situation at his daily conference
with pressmen, the spokesman of
the Foreign Office said Japan con-
sidered that the departure of Gen-
eral Ho Ying-chin for North
China signified that General
Chiang Kai-shek did not want to
discuss affairs there with the
Japanese Ambassador, Mr. Ariyo-
shi.—Reuter.
Two Japanese Said Killed
PEIPING, Dec. 2.—An incident
alleged to have cost the lives of
two Japanese is reported from
Tawangchang, a village situated
east of Tientsin.
The two Japanese are said to
have gathered the villagers to-
gether on Saturday and to have
harangued them on the subject of
autonomy.
The audience, so the story goes,
manhandled the Japanese, who are
reported to have been fatally
wounded.
The report is confirmed in
semi-official sources, but the
Japanese authorities and the vari-
ous newspapers in North China
are silent on the subject.—
Reuter.
A Call On General Tada
TIENTSIN, Dec. 2.—Arriving
here from the capital, obviously
to seek an understanding with the
Japanese military authorities on
the North China visit of General
Ho Ying-chin, Chinese Minister of
War, two Nanking emissaries this
morning were accorded an
interview by General Hayao Tada,
commander of the Nippon forces
in North China.
General Chen I, Chairman of the
Fukien Provincial Government,
and Mr. Yin Tung, former man-
aging director of the Peiping-
Liaoning Railway, arrived here at
8 o'clock this morning. The latter
called alone at General Tada's
office at 9 o'clock.
（批：SI MS 8 DEC 1935）

《字林西报》，1935年12月3日，星期二
军政部长抵达
保定府；立即
进入谈判
消息灵通人士在北平讨论成立拥有五省控制权的北方政治委员会
日本军方对持续的不安定局势感到不耐烦

北平，12月2日电。——今天这里人们询问的一个问题是，被南京政府派往北平担任行政院驻平代表的中国军政部长何应钦将军，能否为中国保住华北五省，或其中的一部分。人们认为，他很有机会组织一种半独立的行政形式，这在很大程度上能满足日本的要求，同时在名义上仍受南京控制。消息灵通的中国人正在讨论成立一个名为“中华民国北方政治委员会”的机构的可能性，该委员会将管辖河北、山东、山西、察哈尔和绥远各省。
有人建议，该委员会应是一个规模较大的机构，成员或许达40人，包括居住在该地区的一些退休北方军阀和官员，但毫无疑问，平津卫戍司令宋哲元将军必须担任委员会主席，因为他是该地区唯一拥有足够兵力维持治安的人。新机构的地位将与蒙古自治委员会类似。
据信，该计划可能会被日本接受。据悉，关东军的土肥原贤二少将已与宋哲元将军进行过讨论，并表示愿意进一步商讨。然而，显而易见的是，解决华北事务刻不容缓。
日本军方发言人今天表示，日本军方当局对华北的不安定局势日益感到不耐烦。
当被问及自治运动时，他说该运动“仍在进展中，但预计不会有立即的发展”。他补充说，如果何应钦将军来到北平，不会与他进行谈判，尽管他可能会拜访日本当局。他补充说，自治将首先实现，然后才可能讨论该地区的行政管理和委员会问题。

北平市长的电报
北平市长秦德纯将军今天致电南京当局，敦促他们制定措施以应对华北局势。
人们认为，秦将军的这一举动，连同天津市长程克先生和宋哲元将军最近的声明，为宣布自治铺平了道路，而他们担心自己将不可避免地被迫这样做。
据一位中国高级官员称，土肥原贤二少已向宋将军暗示，进一步拖延以满足局势和自治派的要求将是困难的。
据报道，宋将军回答说，只要示威活动有序，当局就不会干涉。
宋将军和其他官员正前往河北省会保定府，会见今天抵达那里的何应钦将军。
预计他们将同河北省主席商震将军举行会谈，但鉴于何将军在徐州发表的据报道的声明，他最终是否会来北平尚存疑问。据说他曾表示不确定是否会在北平就任新职。
今天，当被问及有关十列日本军用列车从沈阳抵达山海关的报道时，日本军方发言人宣称他对此事没有任何信息。
关于三个师团的部队正从日本派往华北的持续报道，在此间所有消息灵通人士中均不被采信。——路透社。

自治委员会
南京，12月2日电。——此间消息灵通人士称，平津卫戍司令宋哲元将军建议成立一个河北反共自治委员会，并由他本人担任主席。
另有消息称，这一建议将由军政部长何应钦将军和宋将军进行讨论。——路透社。

程毅将军
天津，12月2日电。——福建省主席程毅将军今晨从南京抵达此处，将于今晚前往北平。
他拒绝接受任何采访，但他前往北平被视为表明华北新政权即将建立。
此处人们相信，正在前往保定府的何将军将在那里停留，直到收到程毅将军的消息后再前往北平。
天津市长程克先生今天从北平返回，并发出多封电报，敦促中国政府主动在华北建立自治政权，以维护中国的主权权利，以此标志其归来。
天津九个自治区的主任和代表已致电南京，敦促中央政府采取有效措施保障河北的安全，并宣称区域自治是解决当前困难的最佳方案。天津中华总商会也发出了类似的电报。——路透社。

不确定是否就职
南京，12月2日电。——据报道，何应钦将军昨天途经徐州时接受采访，告诉新闻界人士，他不确定是否会在北平就任新职。——路透社。

王博士拜会广田
东京，12月2日电。——前南京外交部长王正廷博士今天上午访问了外务省，并与日本外相广田弘毅先生及副相重光葵先生进行了会晤。
外务省发言人在每日记者招待会上讨论中日局势时表示，日本认为何应钦将军前往华北意味着蒋介石将军不想与日本大使有吉明先生讨论那里的事务。——路透社。

两名日本人据称被杀
北平，12月2日电。——据报，在位于天津以东的大王庄（Tawangchang）村发生了一起据称导致两名日本人死亡的事件。
据说这两名日本人于周六召集村民，并就自治问题向他们发表演说。
据称，听众对这两名日本人动了手，导致他们受致命伤。
半官方消息来源证实了这一报道，但日本当局和华北各报纸对此事保持沉默。——路透社。

拜会多田将军
天津，12月2日电。——两名南京特使今晨从首都抵达此处，显然是为了就中国军政部长何应钦将军访问华北一事寻求与日本军方当局的谅解，他们获得了驻华北日军司令多田骏将军的接见。
福建省政府主席陈仪将军和前平宁铁路总经理殷同先生于今晨8时抵达此处。后者于9时单独拜访了多田将军的办公室。
（批：SI MS 1935年12月8日）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 4, 1935    126llc

Ho Reaches Peiping;
Trip Taken Following
Doihara Phone Talks

Conferences On North
China Affairs To Con-
tinue In Old Capital

CHINESE FEEL
SITUATION BETTER

Doihara Working Hard
To Gain Big Area
Without Fight

PEIPING, Dec. 3.—(Reuters).—
General Ho Ying-chin, the Chinese
War Minister, who has been sent
to North China by the Nanking
Government to devise some solution
of the problem arising from the
so-called autonomy movement, arriv-
ed here at 6.35 o'clock this evening.
His arrival followed three drama-
tic telephone conversations that he
had during the night with Major-
General Kenji Doihara, his princi-
pal protagonist in the North China
drama.
General Ho was in Paotingfu, the
seat of the Hopei Provincial Govern-
ment, where he had been conferr-
ing with General Shang Chen, Gov-
ernor of Hopei, and other North
China leaders, and Major-General
Doihara was in Peiping.
"Moderately satisfactory" is the
description given in reliable Chinese
quarters to the conversations, the
first of which took place at 11
o'clock as the result of a call put in
by General Ho. Later, Major-Gen-
eral Doihara called up the War
Minister, and, finally, at 3 o'clock
this morning, General Ho telephon-
ed a second time to the Japanese
officer.
The Minister of War left his
special train at the Paotingfu sta-
tion at 10.30 this morning, arriving
within half an hour at the Hopei
Government offices, where talks took
place with General Shang Chen, offi-
cials and others. At 11.30 General
Ho, accompanied by Mr. Wang
Peng-yang, Secretary of the War
Ministry, and other officials, left
Paotingfu by special train for Peip-
ing, arriving here at 6.35 this even-
ing. He was met at the station by
General Sung Cheh-yuan, Garrison
Commander of Peiping and Tientsin,
and other officials.
General Ho and a number of offi-
cials left by special train for Pao-
tingfu this morning, returning by
another special train this evening.
It is understood that the War Minis-
ter will remain in Peiping for sev-
eral days.
Reports that General Ho had re-
ceived instructions from Nanking to
accept the Japanese demands for au-
tonomy in North China were denied
in responsible quarters. It was stat-
ed that the War Minister's mission
was to seek a solution of the prob-
lem which would be acceptable to
both the Central Government and
the people of North China.

Paotingfu Bustling
With a steady stream of officials
arriving from Peiping, Paotingfu
hummed with activity throughout
the day. Nothing was divulged,
however, concerning the progress of
General Ho's negotiations, although
he was reported to have been again
in telephonic communication with
Peiping.
General Chin Teh-chun, Mayor of
Peiping, today denied the report
that General Sung Cheh-yuan, Gar-
rison Commander of Peiping and
Tientsin, went yesterday to Pao-
tingfu, to which center he was re-
ported to have traveled secretly
to meet General Ho.
General Sung was, however, re-
presented at the provincial seat by
two officials, General Meng Chi-
chung and Mr. Lei Shou-ying. Mr.
Lei, who arrived there this morning,
carried a long report from General
Sung for presentation to General Ho.
Several Japanese, including one
alleged to be an adviser to Mr. Yin
Ju-keng leader of the so-called
autonomous government of East
Hopei, also arrived at Paotingfu
this morning, but up to early this
evening none of them had gained
access to the Chinese War Minis-
ter.
Some alarm was felt by the in-
habitants of Paotingfu this morn-
ing when several Japanese air-
planes made their appearance and
circled over the city. They remain-
ed aloft for several hours.
General Hsiung Shih-hui, chair-
man of the Hopei provincial gov-
ernment, who accompanied General
Ho when he left Nanking for North
China, reached Peiping this morn-
ing.
He follows General Chen Yi,
Governor of Fukien, who also left
Nanking with General Ho, and
who arrived here yesterday from
Tientsin, where he interviewed Lt.-
Gen. [Tashiro], commander of the Jap-
anese troops in North China.

Doihara Working Hard
Well-informed foreign sources de-
clare that Major-General Doihara
is indicated clearly the importance
placed on the outcome of the
task to which he had set his hand
—that of winning for Japan, ac-
tually or practically, a vast slice
of territory without military opera-
tions.
Unquestionably, he is fighting the
hardest diplomatic battle of his
uniformly successful career.
Ten prominent educators, includ-
ing representatives of five universi-
ties, the Academia Sinica, and the
National Library, have despatched
a telegram to the Executive Yuan
at Nanking concerning public feel-
ing in North China.
The message read:
"In the past two days there have
appeared in the press several tele-
grams giving the impression that
there is a public sentiment in North
China for local autonomy.
"From personal observation we
now positively that, despite the
handbills distributed by persons
hired for the purpose, no section of
the population of any profession or
trade has any desire for autonomy
or separation from the Central
Government.
"We hope you will not be misled
by these telegrams. We hope that
both the Central and local authori-
ties will use all the means at their
disposal to maintain territorial and
administrative integrity."

《字林西报》，1935年12月4日，星期三    126llc

何应钦抵达北平；
此行系在与土肥原
通电话后进行

关于华北事务的会议
将在旧都继续举行

中国人感觉
局势好转

土肥原正努力
不战而获取大片区域

北平，12月3日—（路透社）—中国军政部长何应钦将军，奉南京政府之命前往华北，旨在为所谓“自治运动”引发的问题寻求某种解决方案，于今晚6时35分抵达此地。他的到来，紧随其夜间与华北事态中的主要对手土肥原贤二少将进行的三次戏剧性电话交谈之后。

何将军此前在河北省政府所在地保定府，一直与河北省主席商震将军及其他华北领导人进行会谈，而土肥原少将则身处北平。

据可靠的中方人士称，这些谈话“尚属满意”，第一次谈话是何将军主动致电，于11时进行。随后，土肥原少将致电军政部长，最后，何将军于今日凌晨3时再次致电这位日本军官。

军政部长于今天上午10时30分在保定府车站离开专列，半小时内抵达河北省政府办公处，在那里与商震将军、官员及其他人士进行了会谈。11时30分，何将军在军政部秘书王彭阳先生及其他官员的陪同下，乘专列离开保定府前往北平，于今晚6时35分抵达。他在车站受到平津卫戍司令宋哲元将军及其他官员的迎接。

何将军及数名官员今晨乘专列前往保定府，今晚又乘另一列专列返回。据悉，军政部长将在北平停留数日。

有关何将军已收到南京指示、接受日本关于华北自治的要求的报道，被负责方面予以否认。据称，军政部长的使命是寻求一种既能被中央政府接受、又能被华北民众接受的解决方案。

保定府一片繁忙

随着来自北平的官员源源不断地抵达，保定府整天都处于忙碌状态。然而，关于何将军谈判进展的情况未予透露，尽管据报道他再次与北平进行了电话沟通。

北平市市长秦德纯将军今日否认了有关平津卫戍司令宋哲元将军昨日前往保定府的报道，此前有消息称宋将军秘密前往该中心会见何将军。

不过，宋将军由孟继中将军和雷寿荣先生两名官员代表出席省府会议。雷先生于今晨抵达那里，携带了宋将军呈交给何将军的一份长篇报告。

几名日本人，其中包括一名据称是冀东所谓“自治政府”首领殷汝耕顾问的人，也于今晨抵达保定府，但直到今晚早些时候，他们中无人得以面见中国军政部长。

今晨，当几架日本飞机出现并在城市上空盘旋时，保定府居民感到有些恐慌。这些飞机在空中停留了数小时。

陪同何将军离开南京前往华北的河北省政府主席熊式辉将军，于今晨抵达北平。

他紧随福建省主席陈仪将军之后，陈将军也与何将军一同离开南京，并于昨日从天津抵达此处，在天津他会见了日本华北驻屯军司令官[田代]中将。

土肥原正努力工作

消息灵通的外国来源宣称，土肥原少将清楚地表明了对其所承担任务结果的重视——即为日本实际或实质上赢得一大片领土，而无需军事行动。

毫无疑问，他正在其一贯成功的职业生涯中进行最艰难的外交斗争。

十位知名教育家，包括五所大学、中央研究院和国家图书馆的代表，就华北公众情绪向南京行政院发出了一份电报。

电文如下：
“过去两天，报刊上出现了几封电报，给人留下华北存在地方自治公众舆论的印象。
“根据亲身观察，我们现在肯定地指出，尽管有人雇佣散发传单，但任何职业或行业的民众阶层均无自治或与中央政府分离的愿望。
“我们希望你们不要被这些电报误导。我们希望中央和地方当局利用一切可用手段，维护领土和行政完整。”

Peiping Impression That
Events In North Are Now
Heading Towards Crisis

PEIPING MILITARY COUNCIL WINDS UP
ITS AFFAIRS IN ACCORDANCE WITH
INSTRUCTIONS FROM NANKING

SECRET CONFERENCE OF CHINESE
LEADERS LASTS TILL 4 A.M.

Important Telegram Sent To Nanking Asking For
More Specific Instructions; Tokyo Does Not
Intend To Reply To Protest On Seizure

PEIPING, Nov. 30.—The Peiping Military Council wound up its affairs to-day in accordance with instructions from Nanking.

Hereafter, matters previously handled by the Council will be dealt with by the Nanking Military Council.

Meanwhile, there is a general impression that events here are rapidly heading for a crisis, which may come as soon as Monday.

It is learned that a secret conference of local Chinese leaders lasted from last evening till four o'clock this morning, at the conclusion of which an important telegram was dispatched to Nanking asking for more specific instructions.

It is understood that the telegram was addressed to General Chiang Kai-shek, Dr. H. H. Kung, Finance Minister, and General Ho Ying-chin, Minister of war.

According to the Japanese military spokesman, the telegram is to the effect that the autonomy movement developing now is beyond the powers of the local authorities to stop.

Hopei And Chahar Only?

On the other hand, well-informed Chinese sources declare that the Japanese have expressed the view that the autonomy of Hopei and Chahar would satisfy them and that the area might still be nominally under Nanking.

It is reported that Major-General Doihara, who, it was rumoured, had intended to leave to-day, is now remaining for another two or three days.

Chinese Conferences

The chief of staff of General Sung Cheh-yuan, garrison commander of Peiping and Tientsin, who visited Paotingfu on Wednesday to see General Shang Chen, chairman of Hopei, and to invite him to come to Peiping, returned this afternoon, not with General Shang Chen but with his chief of staff.

The latter held a conference with General Sung this evening, but the result is not known.

Loyalty Pledged

Telegrams pledging their loyalty to the Government were sent to Nanking to-day by the Labour Union of Peiping and the Farmers' Union of Hopei Province.

"We swear to remain loyal to our Central Government and to resist any action taken by the puppet regime of the self-styled East Hopei Autonomous Government to consolidate its position," declared the former, while the telegram of the Farmers' Union read, in part:

"We solemnly declare that we denounce the so-called East Hopei Autonomous Government.

"We are determined to have no dealings with the puppet regime, and we are ready to give every support to our Government in the maintenance of territorial integrity in China."—Reuters.

Japan Not To Reply

TOKYO, Nov. 30.—The Japanese Government will not reply to the Chinese protest on the alleged seizure of Fengtai junction by Japanese troops on Thursday, on the ground that such action would be "unnecessary, as the question was already been settled."

This was the statement made today by a spokesman of the Foreign Office, who said that a report on the subject had been received this morning from Mr. A. Ariyoshi, Japanese Ambassador to China.

the part of Chinese authorities to shunt freight cars from the Peiping-Mukden and Suifunho railways to the Peiping-Hankow and the Tientsin-Pukow lines constituted a threat to the maintenance of such traffic.

Threatened Complications

It would also facilitate the sending of Chinees troops northwards thus "threatening further to complicate the situation in North China."

"We sent a number of soldiers to Fengtai to warn the officials there not to allow any freight cars to proceed southwards. When we received an answer, we left a few men to check on traffic movements," he declared.

The official asserted that Mr. Tang Yu-jen, Chinese Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs, had received and accepted an explanation on the subject from Mr. Y. Suma on Friday and that, consequently, he considered the issue closed.

Report From Mr. Ariyoshi

The Foreign Office, he said, was also in receipt of a report from Mr. Ariyoshi on his conversation yesterday with Dr. H. H. Kung, Minister of Finance.

In this interview, Dr. Kung is said to have asked the Ambassador about reports that Japanese officials were taking part in the autonomy movement in North China, whereupon Mr. Ariyoshi was reported to have replied he "regretted" that the Chinese official had made such a remark.

The Ambassador, is his dispatch, said that he had declared that the credence attached to such rumours by Chinese officials was indicative of their "lack of perception of the true state of affairs in North China."

A Remonstrance

Moreover, he continued, he had remonstrated to Dr. Kung on the manner in which the Chinese Government had ordered personnel changes in North China without first consulting with the Japanese authorities as had been promised to him by Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek in their interview on November 20.

Mr. Ariyoshi also added that he had refused a request for Japanese participation in a loan to China on the ground that the time was "inopportune."—Rengo.

Japanese Troops Checking Trains

PEIPING, Nov. 30.—The few remaining Japanese troops at the Fengtai railway station continued to have to busy day to-day checking all incoming and outgoing trains and rolling stock that pass through the railroad depot, according to information from Fengtai.

It is learned that passenger trains were permitted to proceed southward after checking but railway coaches on the Peiping-Liaoning line were not allowed to be transferred to the Peiping-Hankow railway.

Meanwhile, it is reported that the Peiping-Liaoning Railway Administration has sent instructions to various station masters along the line to the effect that all precautionary measures be taken to ensure safety in travelling along the line.—Central News.

Sung Issues Second
Telegram

TIENTSIN, Nov. 30.—General Sung Cheh-yuan, garrison commander of the Peiping-Tientsin Area, issued a second circular telegram at 8 o'clock this evening to the effect that the provinces of Hopei and Chahar, and the cities of Peiping and Tientsin should form "as soon as possible" an autonomous State, a telephonic message from Peiping said.

The message, which was addressed to the leaders of the Nanking Government, was said to declare that the situation in North China could no longer be ignored and that if the central Government did not take immediate steps to meet the demands of the people, the local authorities would be compelled to take action themselves.

北平印象：
华北事态正走向危机

北平军事委员会奉南京指令
结束其事务

中国领导人秘密会议
持续至凌晨4时

发出重要电报致南京请求更具体指示；东京无意就扣押事件回复抗议

北平，11月30日电。——北平军事委员会今日奉南京指令结束其事务。

此后，原由该委员会处理之事项将改由南京军事委员会处理。

与此同时，普遍印象认为此地事态正迅速走向危机，危机最早可能于星期一爆发。

据悉，当地中国领导人的秘密会议从昨晚持续至今日凌晨四时，会议结束后发出一封重要电报致南京，请求更具体的指示。

据了解，该电报系发给蒋介石将军、财政部长孔祥熙博士以及军政部长何应钦将军。

据日本军方发言人称，该电报大意是，目前发展的自治运动已超出地方当局制止的能力范围。

仅河北与察哈尔？

另一方面，消息灵通的中国方面人士宣称，日本人表示，若河北和察哈尔实现自治即可满足其要求，且该地区名义上仍可归属南京管辖。

据报道，传闻原定今日离开的土肥原贤二少将（Major-General Doihara）现在决定再停留两三天。

中方会议

驻守北平和天津的司令官宋哲元将军的参谋长，周三前往保定府会见河北省主席商震将军并邀请其来北平，于今日下午返回，但并非与商震将军同行，而是与其参谋长一同返回。

后者今晚与宋将军举行了会议，但结果尚不清楚。

宣誓效忠

北平工会和河北省农会今日向南京发送了宣誓效忠政府的电报。

前者宣称：“我们誓死效忠中央政府，并抵抗所谓‘冀东自治政府’傀儡政权为巩固其地位所采取的任何行动，”而农会的电报部分内容如下：

“我们郑重声明，我们谴责所谓的‘冀东自治政府’。

“我们决心不与该傀儡政权进行任何往来，并准备全力支持我国政府维护中国领土完整。”——路透社。

日本不予回复

东京，11月30日电。——日本政府将不会就中方针对日军周四 allegedly（据称）占领丰台站一事提出的抗议作出回复，理由是此举“没有必要，因为该问题已经解决”。

这是外交部发言人今日发表的声明，他表示今晨已收到日本驻华大使有吉明（A. Ariyoshi）先生关于此事的报告。

中国当局将北宁铁路和绥芬河铁路的货运车厢调往平汉线和津浦线，构成了对维持此类交通的威胁。

威胁引发复杂局势

此举也将便于中国军队向北调动，从而“进一步使华北局势复杂化”。

“我们派遣了一些士兵前往丰台，警告当地官员不得允许任何货运车厢向南行驶。当我们得到答复后，我们留下少数人员检查交通动向，”他宣称。

该官员断言，中国外交部次长唐有壬先生已于周五收到并接受须磨弥吉郎（Y. Suma）先生就此事的解释，因此他认为该问题已告终结。

来自有吉先生的报告

他说，外交部还收到了有吉先生关于昨日与财政部长孔祥熙博士会谈的报告。

在此次会晤中，据说孔博士询问大使有关日本官员参与华北自治运动的报道，随后据报道有吉先生回答说，他对这位中国官员发表此类言论表示“遗憾”。

大使在其发回的电文中称，他曾声明，中国官员轻信此类谣言表明他们“缺乏对华北真实局势的认知”。

提出抗议

此外，他继续说道，他还就中国政府在未事先与日本当局协商的情况下下令变更华北人事安排一事向孔博士提出抗议，尽管蒋介石委员长在11月20日的会晤中曾向他承诺会进行协商。

有吉先生还补充说，他以时机“不适宜”为由，拒绝了日本参与对华贷款的要求。——联合通讯社。

日军检查列车

北平，11月30日电。——据来自丰台的消息，驻丰台火车站的少量剩余日军今日继续忙碌，检查所有进出并通过该铁路站场的列车及车辆。

据悉，客运列车经检查后获准向南行驶，但北宁线上的铁路客车不被允许转移至平汉铁路。

与此同时，据报道，北宁铁路管理局已向沿线各站长发出指示，要求采取一切预防措施，以确保沿线旅行安全。——中央通讯社。

宋发出第二封
电报

天津，11月30日电。——据来自北平的电话消息，平津卫戍司令宋哲元将军于今晚8时发出第二封通电解，大意是河北、察哈尔两省及北平、天津两市应“尽快”组成一个自治邦。

据悉，该致南京政府领导人的电文宣称，华北局势已不能再被忽视，如果中央政府不立即采取措施满足民众要求，地方当局将被迫自行采取行动。

共和国被接管

北平，11月30日电。——所谓“冀东自治政府”的代表昨日接管了通县地区的行政管理工作，今日抵达此处并...

pages.en:
FOR FIRST TIME OF AUTONOMY
MOVEMENT IN NORTHERN CHINA

General Ho Ying-chin,
War Minister, Leaves
Nanking For Peiping

DEPARTURE INTERPRETED AS DEFINITE
SIGN OF GOVERNMENT'S RESOLVE
TO DEAL WITH SITUATION

GEN. SUNG CHEH-YUAN EXPRESSES HIS
INABILITY TO CONTROL MOVEMENT

Feeling Of Despair In Peiping; Japan Requests
Railway Facilities For Troops Being Shifted
From Shanhaikwan To Tientsin

TIENTSIN, Dec. 1.—Mr. Cheng Keh, Mayor of Tien-
tsin, to-night sent a circular telegram to the Nanking
authorities asking them "to take immediate appropriate
measures."
The message, which was sent at 10.30 o'clock, declared
that unless a remedy was offered by the National Govern-
ment, "the Tientsin Special Municipality would be com-
pelled to proclaim autonomy."—Rengo.

PEIPING, Dec. 1.—The first Chinese official admission of
the existence of an autonomy movement in North China was
made yesterday by General Sung Cheh-yuan, garrison com-
mander of Peiping and Tientsin.
In a telegram to Nanking, he referred to a growing
movement among the people favouring autonomy, and
expressed his inability to control the movement by mere
empty words.
General Sung added that unless more effective measures
were devised for satisfying the longing of the people and
pacifying their minds, the internal situation would become
more serious, apart from external difficulties.
Considerable importance is at-
tached by Chinese circles to this
telegram, as it is the first official
admission of an autonomy move-
ment in North China.

GENERAL HO YING-CHIN

In the meantime, while the pub-
lic welcomes the news that Gen-
eral Ho Ying-chin, the War Minis-
ter, is coming north, there is a
feeling that the situation here has
gone so far that he can do very
little to improve affairs.
A Surprising Move
In fact, the news of the War
Minister's departure from the
capital has been generally receiv-
ed with surprise, as it had been
felt that his appointment here was

华北自治运动
首次出现

军政部长何应钦将军
离开南京前往北平

此行被解读为政府决意
处理局势的明确信号

宋哲元将军表示
无力控制该运动

北平弥漫绝望情绪；日本要求为从山海关调往天津的部队提供铁路便利

天津，12月1日电。——天津市市长程克今晚向南京当局发出通电解，请求他们“立即采取适当措施”。

该于10时30分发出的电文宣称，除非国民政府提供补救办法，“天津特别市将被迫宣布自治”。——联合通讯社。

北平，12月1日电。——中国官方首次承认华北存在自治运动，是由北平和天津卫戍司令宋哲元将军于昨日作出的。

他在致南京的电报中提到，民众中支持自治的运动日益增长，并表示他无法仅凭空话控制该运动。

宋将军补充说，除非制定更有效的措施来满足民众的愿望并安抚民心，否则除了外部困难外，内部局势也将变得更加严峻。

中国各界对此电报相当重视，因为这是官方首次承认华北存在自治运动。

何应钦将军

与此同时，虽然公众对军政部长何应钦将军北上的消息表示欢迎，但也有一种感觉认为，这里的局势已发展到如此地步，他能改善局面的余地很小。

令人惊讶的举动

事实上，军政部长离开首都的消息普遍引起惊讶，因为人们原本觉得他在此地的任命注定是一个永远不会...
如果何将军能为中央政府保住河北，那他确实是从火海中挽救了它...

即使在日本人中间，也只有官员仍声称宋哲元将军没有受到外部压力。

各界都怀着浓厚兴趣等待何将军明早抵达。

行踪成谜

但军政部长的当前行踪 somewhat（有点）是个谜。

据报道，他在济南下车去见山东省主席韩复榘将军，而一些官员已从此地前往保定府，期望在他来北平之前在那里见到他。

另有报道称，他根本不会来这里。——路透社。

何应钦将军离开
南京，12月1日电。——军政部长兼最近任命的行政院驻北平代表何应钦将军，昨晚乘火车前往北平。

他前往北平之举在此地普遍受到欢迎，被视为政府决意处理华北局势的明确迹象。

由于何将军在新任命后延迟出发，这里此前一段时间曾感到些许担忧，因为人们认为，在当前危急时刻，北方没有任何南京重要官员在场会导致阴谋和混乱。

人们普遍承认，何将军的任务并不令人羡慕，对他成功的希望非常渺茫。然而，他突然决定北上，首先表明中国人并未放弃解决华北局势的希望，并积极寻求解决方案；其次表明北方局势如此紧迫，何将军立即亲临北平至关重要。——路透社。

有吉明先生取消
南京之行

据联合通讯社昨晚报道，原定昨晚11时启程前往南京的日本驻华大使有吉明（Akira Ariyoshi）先生，突然于8时15分取消了既定行程。

未能获悉计划变更的原因。

（批注：已阅 1935年12月3日）

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 30, 1935

Deserter Of
Yin's "Regime"
Explains Role

Ho Shih Says He Joined
Temporarily To Insure
His Own Safety

NANKING SCHOLARS
URGE SUPPRESSION

Shang Chen Says He Is
Doing All Possible
To Oust Usurpers

NANKING, Nov. 29.—(Reuters).—
Mr. Ho Shih, resident representa-
tive of the Government at Kupei-
kow, in the Luantung Demilitarized
Zone, who arrived here from Pei-
ping last night, explained today
how he became one of those who
participated in the inauguration of
the "East Hopei Autonomous Gov-
ernment."
It was, he said, a ruse to ensure
his personal safety.
Mr. Yin Ju-keng, the self-pro-
claimed head of the movement, on
November 25 summoned him to
Tungchow, where he was forced to
sign the declaration of autonomy.
Subsequently, Mr. Ho Shih pro-
ceeded. Mr. Yin sent him on a
mission to Peiping, where, imme-
diately upon arriving, he issued a
statement repudiating his connec-
tion with the autonomous regime.
Mr. Ho called on officials of the
Executive Yuan today, to whom he
submitted a report on the Tung-
chow affair.

Waichiaopu Issues Communique
NANKING, Nov. 29.—(Central).—
In a communique today, the Wai-
chiaopu has notified all diplomatic
envoys stationed in China that all
action taken by Yin Yu-keng, ring-
leader of the so-called "Autonomous
Movement" in east Hopei, must be
considered as null and void.
Chinese diplomatic representatives
abroad were also today instructed
by the Waichiaopu to serve similar
notices to the respective Govern-
ments to which they are accredited.

"Foreign Minister" In Nanking
Mr. Ho Shih, former director of
the Kapeikow office of the Luan-
chow-Shanhaikwan area who has
disassociated himself with the so-
called "Eastern Hopei Autonomous
Council" by refusing to accept the
post as director of foreign affairs
of the bogus organisation, arrived
here from Peiping yesterday. He
was accompanied by Mr. Yin Ti-
yang, nephew of Yin Ju-keng, chair-
man of the bogus council, who is
opposed to his uncle's treacherous
acts.
Mr. Ho made a verbal report to
Mr. Peng Hsueh-pei, Director of
Political Affairs of the Executive
Yuan on Yin's rebellion this morn-
ing.
In a press interview today Mr. Ho
stated the conditions in Kupeikow
were confused with the movements
of the Japanese troops along the
Great Wall. Before his departure
from Kupeikow, he said, 3,000 Japan-
ese troops had already arrived there
and the town was occupied by the
Japanese troops.

《字林西报》，1935年11月30日，星期六

殷氏“政权”之逃兵
解释其角色

何世（音译）称其加入
仅为暂时之举以确保
自身安全

南京学者
呼吁镇压

商震称正尽一切可能
驱逐篡位者

南京，11月29日.—（路透社）.—
滦东非军事区古北口政府驻派代表何世（音译）先生昨晚从北平抵达此处，今日解释了他是如何成为参与 inaugurating “冀东自治政府”的人员之一的。
他说，这是一种确保个人安全的权宜之计。
自称该运动首领的殷汝耕先生于11月25日将他召至通州，在那里他被迫签署自治宣言。
随后，何世（音译）先生启程。殷先生派他前往北平执行任务，他抵达后立即发表声明，否认与自治政权的关联。
何先生今日拜会了行政院官员，并向他们提交了关于通州事件的报告。

外交部发布公报
南京，11月29日.—（中央社）.—
外交部在今日的一份公报中通知所有驻华外交使节，冀东所谓“自治运动”头目殷汝耕所采取的一切行动必须被视为无效。
外交部今日也指示中国驻外外交代表向各自派驻国政府发出类似通知。

“外交部长”在南京
前滦州-山海关地区古北口办事处主任何世（音译）先生，因拒绝接受该伪组织的外交处长职务而与所谓“冀东自治委员会”划清界限，昨日从北平抵达此处。陪同他的是伪委员会主席殷汝耕的侄子殷体扬（音译）先生，他反对伯父的叛国行径。
何先生今晨向行政院政务处处长彭学沛先生口头汇报了殷氏叛乱情况。
何先生在今日接受记者采访时称，随着日军沿长城调动，古北口的局势陷入混乱。他说，在他离开古北口之前，已有3,000名日军抵达那里，该镇已被日军占领。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 30, 1935

Nanking Files Vigorous
Protest With Japan On
Happenings In N. China

Alleged Participation Of Japanese Officers In The
Autonomy Movement Definitely Mentioned And
Evacuation Of Stations Asked For

HINT THAT JAPANESE AUTHORITIES MIGHT
NEGOTIATE WITH SUNG CHEH-YUAN

NANKING, Nov. 29.—Charging that the autonomy movement in North China was engineered by “disgruntled elements acting in connivance with Japanese military officers,” the Nanking Government to-day filed two vigorous protests with Japan. The first of these protested against the alleged participation of Japanese officers in the autonomy movement, and asked the Japanese Government to curb their activities.

The other representation protested against the occupation of the Fengtai and Changyimen railway stations in the vicinity of Peiping, on the ground that it constituted a violation of China’s sovereignty. The two Notes were handed by the Waichiachpu to Mr. Yakichiro Suma, Japanese Consul-General here. The Chinese Government stressed its desire to settle the Northern problems through diplomatic channels, and asserted that the autonomy movement did not represent “popular desires.” The second Note asked for the immediate and complete evacuation of the two stations, and for a guarantee against the recurrence of similar incidents.
—Rengo.

PEIPING, Nov. 29.—An appeal to General Ho Ying-chin, the Chinese War Minister, to come to Peiping immediately to take charge of the North China situation is understood to have been telegraphed to Nanking by General Sun Cheh-yuan, Garrison Commander of Peiping and Tientsin, following an important conference of North China officials here this morning.

At the same time General Sung declined to reconsider his decision not to accept the post of Pacification Commissioner for Hopei and Chahar, which he has rejected on the ground that the responsibility involved is too great.

Those attending the conference included General Chin Teh-chun, Mayor of Peiping; General Hsiao Cheng-yin, Governor of Chahar, and General Chang Tze-chun, acting Governor of Chahar, who arrived in Peiping only this morning.

The subject of autonomy inevitably loomed large at the meeting, but reports that the question was actually discussed cannot be authoritatively confirmed.

Pressure On Gen. Sung

Chinese officials admit, however, that the Japanese military authorities are pressing General Sung to declare his position in regard to autonomy, and say that he cannot wait much longer for a definite lead from Nanking.

General Sung to-day sent his chief counsellor to Paoting to urge General Shang Chen, Governor of Hopei, to come here to confer with him. It is understood that no definite decision on the autonomy question will be made until General Shang’s views have been heard.

Meanwhile, considerable importance is being attached here to the departure for Shansi of General Hsu Yung-chang, Governor of that province.

General Hsu has been conferring here with General Sung

The Gaimusho official expressed regret that the British Government was misled by incorrect press report, adding that the developments in North China were China’s domestic affair, Japan being interested in them only as a neighbour.

Mr. Shigemitsu has also called the attention of Mr. Wiggin to the fact that the actions of Sir Frederick Leith-Ross, chief economic adviser to the British Government, created the impression that he was interfering in China’s internal affairs in connection with his part in the introduction of currency reforms. —Rengo.

Forced To Sign

NANKING, Nov. 29. Mr. Ho Shih, resident representative of the Government at Kalgan, in the Luantung Demilitarized Zone, who arrived here from Peiping last night, explained to-day how he became one of those who participated in the inauguration of the “East Hopei Autonomous Government.”

It was, he said, a ruse to ensure his personal safety.

Mr. Yin Ju-ken, the self-proclaimed head of the movement, on November 25 summoned him to Tungchow, where he was forced to sign the declaration of autonomy.

Subsequently, Mr. Ho Shih proceeded, Mr. Yin sent him on a mission to Peiping, where, immediately upon arriving, he issued a statement repudiating his connection with the autonomous regime.

Mr. Ho called on officials of the Executive Yuan to-day, to whom he submitted a report on the Tungchow affair.—Reuter’s Pacific Service.

Local Parleys

TOKYO, Nov. 29.—Localization of negotiations on the settlement of the problems of North China, while conversations on the broad principles of Sino-Japanese relations are continued in Nanking, is being considered by the Japanese Government, Rengo learned to-day from authoritative sources.

As the Central Government continues to delay the settlement of the Northern issues, negotiations on these questions will now be carried on with General Sung Cheh-yuan, Commander of the Peiping-Tientsin Garrison, Gaimusho officials told Rengo.

At the same time Mr. Ariyoshi, Japanese Ambassador to China, will soon be instructed to continue his negotiations with the Central authorities on the basis of the “three-point programme” of Mr. Hirota, Foreign Minister.

Gaimusho officials point out that in his interview with Mr. Ariyoshi General Chiang Kai-shek, Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission, promised to present shortly a set of concrete proposals for the general readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations.

He has also promised, they added, that General Chiang Tso-pin, Chinese Ambassador to Tokyo now on a furlough, would confer with Mr. Ariyoshi on Mr. Hirota’s programme.

So far, Galmusho officials declared, the Nanking Government has taken no practical steps in carrying out these promises, its only action being the appointment of General Ho Ying-chin, War Minister, as the Executive Yuan’s representative in Peiping.

The situation in North China has reached the stage, the officials continued, when Japan can no longer remain indifferent. North China’s propinquity to Manchoukuo and Japan’s important interests in the area impel the Government to take up the matter directly with General Sung, who controls the region, they pointed out.—Rengo.

Cheh-yuan on North China affairs, and it is understood that he will communicate the latter’s views to General Yen Hsi-shan, Pacification Commissioner of Shansi, who is shortly calling a conference of high officials at Taiyuanfu, the latest developments in North China and Shansi’s attitude towards them.

It is reported that Major-General Doihara, of the Kwantung Army, who had at first planned to visit General Yen, has now requested General Hsu to ascertain his attitude towards the question of autonomy. General Hsu is expected to return to Peiping in about a fortnight.—Reuter.

Favours Direct Negotiation

TOKYO, Nov. 29.—A hint that Japan was prepared to abandon her official attitude of non-interference in North China’s affairs was given by the Foreign Office spokesman to-day.

He stated that, if General Sung Cheh-yuan accepted the post of Pacification Commissioner for Hopei and Chahar, he saw no reason why the Japanese Government should hesitate to negotiate with him regarding the autonomy movement, which affected both Japan and Manchoukuo.—Reuter.

Gaimusho Questioned

TOKYO, Nov. 29.—Information on Japan’s attitude towards the autonomy movement in North China was sought on Wednesday by Mr. Arthur Wiggin, Charge d’Affaires of the British Embassy, in an interview with Mr. Mamoru Shigemitsu, Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs.

Indicating that he was acting on instructions from London, the British official questioned Mr. Shigemitsu on the current reports that Japanese military authorities in North China are supporting the movement for autonomy.

《上海泰晤士报》，1935年11月30日，星期六

南京就华北事态
向日本提出强烈抗议

明确提及日本军官涉嫌参与
自治运动并要求撤出车站

暗示日本当局可能与宋哲元谈判

南京，11月29日.— 南京政府指责华北自治运动是由“与日本军官勾结的不满分子策划的”，今日向日本提出两项强烈抗议。第一项抗议针对日本军官涉嫌参与自治运动，并要求日本政府遏制其活动。

另一项照会抗议日军占领北平附近的丰台和长辛店火车站，理由是这构成了对中国主权的侵犯。这两份照会由外交部交给在此的日本总领事须磨弥吉郎（Yakichiro Suma）先生。中国政府强调希望通过外交渠道解决北方问题，并断言自治运动并不代表“民意”。第二份照会要求立即完全撤出这两个车站，并保证不再发生类似事件。
—联合通讯社。

北平，11月29日.— 据悉，在北平今晨举行重要的华北官员会议后，北平天津卫戍司令孙传芳（Sun Cheh-yuan，注：此处原文为Sun Cheh-yuan，但根据历史语境及后文Sung Cheh-yuan，应指宋哲元，然原文拼写为Sun，依规则保留或按常见译名校正？规则3说能确定的用当时通行中文。Sun Cheh-yuan 极可能是 Sung Cheh-yuan 的OCR错误或笔误，因为后文多次出现 Sung Cheh-yuan 且身份一致。鉴于规则4提到OCR错误照实译出或标不清，但此处明显是同一人。然而规则3要求不确定保留原文。考虑到 "Sun" 和 "Sung" 在威妥玛拼音中不同，但历史上宋哲元为 Sung Cheh-yuan。若严格按原文 Sun Cheh-yuan 翻译为孙传芳则与史实严重不符（孙传芳此时已下野且不在该职）。结合上下文 "General Sung" 反复出现，此处 "Sun" 应为 "Sung" 之误。作为专业译者，应识别此为OCR/排版错误并译为正确人名宋哲元，或在不确定时保留。鉴于后文明确写为 Sung Cheh-yuan，此处判定为印刷错误，译为宋哲元更为妥当，但若严格遵循“照实译出”，则需斟酌。规则4说“明显是OCR遗留的乱码...不要脑补”。这里不是乱码，是拼写差异。为了准确性，我将依据上下文将其统一为宋哲元，因为这是同一篇报道中的同一个人物。但如果必须严格对应文字，Sun是孙。让我们看下文：“General Sung declined...”。上文是“General Sun Cheh-yuan... Garrison Commander”。这是同一个人。因此译为宋哲元。）*修正思考：规则4说“明显是OCR遗留的乱码...照实译出或标（原文不清）”。Sun和Sung是不同的姓。但在这种档案中，混用很常见。为了保险，如果我不确定是否是笔误，我应该保留吗？不，历史背景知识告诉我这是宋哲元。规则3说“能确定的用当时通行的中文”。我能确定这是宋哲元吗？是的，因为职位是北平天津卫戍司令。所以译为宋哲元。*

据理解，北平天津卫戍司令宋哲元将军在今晨于此地举行重要的华北官员会议后，已向南京发电报，呼吁中国军政部部长何应钦将军立即前来北平，主持华北局势。

与此同时，宋将军拒绝重新考虑其不接受冀察绥靖专员一职的决定，他此前以责任过大为由拒绝了该职位。

出席会议者包括北平市市长秦德纯将军、察哈尔省主席萧振瀛将军，以及今晨刚抵达北平的察哈尔省代理主席张自忠将军。

自治问题在会议上不可避免地占据重要地位，但有关该问题实际得到讨论的报道无法得到权威证实。

施压宋将军

中国官员承认，日本军方当局正向宋将军施压，要求他就自治问题表明立场，并称他不能无限期等待南京的明确指示。

宋将军今日派遣其首席顾问前往保定，敦促河北省主席商震将军前来此地与他会晤。据悉，在听取商将军的意见之前，不会对自治问题做出任何明确决定。

与此同时，此地高度重视山西省主席徐永昌将军前往山西之行。

徐将军一直在此与宋

外务省官员表示遗憾，英国政府被不实的新闻报道所误导，并补充说，华北的事态是中国的内政，日本仅作为邻国对此感兴趣。

重光葵先生还提请威金（Wiggin）先生注意，英国政府首席经济顾问弗雷德里克·李滋-罗斯爵士（Sir Frederick Leith-Ross）的行动给人留下了这样的印象：即他在推行货币改革的过程中干涉了中国内政。 —联合通讯社。

被迫签字

南京，11月29日。 滦东非军事区张家口政府驻派代表何世（音译）先生昨晚从北平抵达此处，今日解释了他是如何成为参与 inaugurating “冀东自治政府”的人员之一的。

他说，这是一种确保个人安全的权宜之计。

自称该运动首领的殷汝耕先生于11月25日将他召至通州，在那里他被迫签署自治宣言。

随后，何世（音译）先生启程。殷先生派他前往北平执行任务，他抵达后立即发表声明，否认与自治政权的关联。

何先生今日拜会了行政院官员，并向他们提交了关于通州事件的报告。—路透社太平洋分社。

地方会谈

东京，11月29日.— 联合通讯社今日从权威渠道获悉，日本政府正在考虑将解决华北问题的谈判局部化，而在南京继续就中日关系广泛原则进行对话的同时。

由于中央政府继续拖延解决北方问题，外务省官员告诉联合通讯社，现在将与北平天津卫戍司令宋哲元将军就这些问题进行谈判。

同时，日本驻华大使有吉明（Ariyoshi）先生不久将接到指示，继续以外相广田弘毅先生的“三点计划”为基础与中央当局进行谈判。

外务省官员指出，蒋介石委员长（军事委员会委员长）在与有吉先生会晤时，承诺不久将提出一套关于全面调整中日关系的具体建议。

他们补充说，他还承诺，目前正在休假的驻东京中国大使蒋作宾将军将就广田先生的计划与有吉先生进行磋商。

外务省官员宣称，到目前为止，南京政府在履行这些承诺方面尚未采取实际行动，其唯一行动是任命军政部部长何应钦将军为行政院驻北平代表。

官员们继续说，华北局势已达到日本不能再漠不关心的阶段。他们指出，华北与满洲国的邻近关系以及日本在该地区的重要利益，促使政府直接与控制该地区的宋将军交涉此事。—联合通讯社。

哲元讨论华北事务，据悉他将把宋将军的观点转达给山西绥靖专员阎锡山将军，阎将军即将在太原府召开高级官员会议，讨论华北最新事态及山西对此的态度。

据报道，关东军土肥原贤二（Doihara）少将起初计划拜访阎将军，现已请求徐将军查明他对自治问题的态度。预计徐将军将在约两周后返回北平。—路透社。

赞成直接谈判

东京，11月29日.— 外交部发言人今日暗示，日本准备放弃其在华北事务中不干涉的官方立场。

他表示，如果宋哲元将军接受冀察绥靖专员一职，他认为日本政府没有理由犹豫不就自治运动与他进行谈判，因为该运动影响日本和满洲国。—路透社。

质询外务省

东京，11月29日.— 英国大使馆代办阿瑟·威金（Arthur Wiggin）先生于周三在与外务次官重光葵先生的会晤中，询问了日本对华北自治运动的态度。

这位英国官员表示他是奉伦敦之命行事，并就当前关于华北日本军方当局支持自治运动的报道向重光先生提出质询。

Gen. Sung Again Declines
PEIPING, Nov. 29.--Gen. Sung
Cheh-yuan, Commander of the
Peiping-Tientsin Garrison, yester-
day again turned down the request
of General Chiang Kai-shek,
Chairman of the Military Affairs
Commission, to accept the post of
the Pacification Commissioner of
Hopei and Chahar.--Rengo.

Tax Bureau Taken Over
TIENTSIN, Nov. 29.--More
than 30 officials of the Consolidat-
ed Tax Bureau at Tongshan ar-
rived here to-day following the
seizure of the office by appointees
of Mr. Yin Ju-keng, who on
Monday created the "East Hopei
Autonomous Council."--Rengo.

Mr. Ariyoshi's Instructions
Acting upon instructions from
the Tokyo Foreign Office, Mr. A.
Ariyoshi, Japanese Ambassador to
China, has decided to proceed to
Nanking in a day or two to discuss
with the Chinese authorities
pending Sino-Japanese issues, the
Central News Agency learned
from the Japanese Embassy here
to-day.
The authorities of the Embassy
denied the press report that the
Japanese ambassador will here-
after be stationed in the capital.
--Central News.

宋将军再次拒绝
北平，11月29日.-- 北平天津卫戍司令宋哲元将军昨日再次拒绝了军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军要求其接受冀察绥靖专员一职的请求。--联合通讯社。

税务局被接管
天津，11月29日.-- 在周一成立“冀东自治委员会”的殷汝耕先生任命的人员接管办公室后，唐山统税局的30多名官员今日抵达此处。--联合通讯社。

有吉先生的指示
据本社今日从日本大使馆获悉，遵照东京外务省的指示，日本驻华大使有吉明（A. Ariyoshi）先生决定在一两天内前往南京，与中国当局讨论 pending 的中日问题。
大使馆当局否认了新闻界关于日本大使此后将常驻首都的报道。
--中央通讯社。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 29, 1935

Nearly All Japanese Are
Withdrawn From Stations
At Fengtai, Changyimen

FEW MEN LEFT BEHIND TO CHECK THE
MOVEMENT OF ROLLING STOCK FOR
FEAR OF ITS REMOVAL SOUTH

JAPAN DOES NOT WISH FOR WAR; HOPES
CHINA IS NOT PREPARING FOR IT

General Sung Cheh-yuan Declines To Take Up
Pacification Post For Chahar And Hopei;
Tokyo Says Movement Is Internal Affair

PEIPING, Nov. 28.—The Japanese military spokesman here, questioned to-day concerning the situation at Fengtai and Changyimen, the two railway stations occupied yesterday by Japanese troops, said that the main forces there were withdrawn this morning, but a few men had been left behind to check the movement of rolling stock.

The spokesman said that, despite Chinese denials that rolling stock was being withdrawn from North China, the Japanese believed that such evacuation was proceeding. They also believed that one third of the rolling stock of the Peiping-Hankow Railway was now concentrated south of the Yellow River.

The Japanese, he continued, knew that there were 1,300 cars on the northern section of the line on November 15, but, 10 days later, this number had been reduced to 900.

Asked the reason why the Japanese were so concerned over the alleged removal of rolling stock to the south, the spokesman said that the withdrawal looked like preparation for war.

“We don’t wish for war,” he declared, “and we hope China doesn’t prepare for war.”

The spokesman denied that the Japanese themselves had actually prevented any rolling stock being moved, saying that the local authorities did not wish any stock to be evacuated and so had stopped the evacuation.

Surprise In Peiping

The withdrawal of the Japanese troops from Fengtai and Changyimen came as a surprise to Peiping in view of the statement by the Japanese military spokesman yesterday that the two stations had been occupied “to protect communications and prevent the removal southward of Peiping of rolling stock.”

Fengtai is an important junction 12 miles south of Peiping, while Changyimen is situated about 300 yards outside the south-west gate of the city.—Reuter.

Change In Status Expected

PEIPING, Nov. 28.—General Sung Cheh-yuan, garrison commander of Peiping and Tientsin, who has just declined the new appointment of Pacification Commissioner for Hopei and Chahar, is being subjected to terrific Japanese pressure, according to reliable Chinese sources.

Well-informed observers, foreign as well as Chinese, believe that the present situation cannot long be maintained, and they voice the opinion that before many days the status of Hopei and Chahar is likely to undergo a change.

It is widely reported to-day that an invitation from General Sung to General Han Fu-chu, chairman of the Shantung Provincial Government, and General Shang Chen, chairman of Hopei, to come to Peiping to discuss the situation has been turned down.

Meanwhile, there is a feeling among those close to General Sung that he has declined his new post because the appointment has come too late.

These circles point out that if the appointment had been made two months ago, the present situation in North China could have been avoided.

It is also stated that General Sung desires rather more authority than the latest appointment would give him, meaning that he probably thinks the appointment should also carry the provincial chairmanship of Hopei, which would enable him to replace the troops of General Shang Chen in Tientsin with his own.—Reuter.

Sung Cheh-yuan Declines Post

NANKING, Nov. 28.—General Sung Cheh-yuan, garrison commander of Peiping and Tientsin, who was appointed by the Nanking Government on Tuesday to be Pacification Commissioner for Hopei and Chahar, has declined to accept the new post.

In a telegram addressed to General Ho Ying-chin, the Minister of War, General Sung declared that he was incapable of shouldering such a heavy responsibility.

“Since it is already difficult to safeguard the security of Peiping and Tientsin,” he added, “I fear that I cannot undertake the heavier responsibility of pacifying Hopei and Chahar.”

In reply, General Ho has telegraphed urging General Sung to assume his new post immediately.—Reuter.

Railway Authorities

PEIPING, Nov. 28. Japanese military representatives here and in Tientsin called the attention of the Peiping-Mukden and the Tientsin-Pukow railways to-day to the fact that a continued removal of the rolling stock south seriously affects the welfare of North China. Lieut.-Col. Tan Takahashi, Japanese assistant military attache stationed here, informed the authorities of the Peiping-Mukden Railway that the withdrawal of freight carriages by the Nanking Government menaces the economic foundations of the region, seriously affects its communications, and aids the outflow of silver southward. Reuter.

“Internal Affair” Says Tokyo

TOKYO, Nov. 28. Questioned by foreign correspondents, the spokesman of the Foreign Office said to-day that the autonomy movement in North China was “a spontaneous campaign by the people, an entirely internal affair in which the Japanese Government had no intention to interfere.”

The spokesman alleged the movement had been “stimulated” by the currency reforms introduced by Nanking.

The British Charge d’Affaires called on the Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs, Mr. Shigemitsu, yesterday afternoon and exchanged information with him concerning the situation in North China. Reuter.

Dr. C. T. Wang In Japan

KOBE, Nov. 28.—Dr. C. T. Wang, formerly Minister for Foreign Affairs at Nanking, arrived here to-day en route to Tokyo.

Interviewed, Dr. Wang denied the rumour that he was on a special mission on behalf of General Chiang Kai-shek.

It is reported, however, that he intends to interview Mr. Hirota, the Japanese Foreign Minister, Mr. Matsuoka, president of the South Manchuria Railway, and other Japanese leaders during his stay in Tokyo, which will last a week.—Reuter.

Kung Confers With Suma

Japan’s attitude towards the North China situation and the recent currency reforms were the major subjects of a 30-minute discussion between Dr. H. H. Kung, Chinese Minister of Finance, and Mr. Y. Suma, Japanese Consul-General in Nanking, on Wednesday night according to the Shanghai “Nippo.”

Replying to Dr. Kung’s request that Japan take a “cautious attitude” in relation to events in the North, Mr. Suma was quoted by the daily as saying that “Japan has nothing to do with the autonomy movement, which is purely an internal issue.”

“However, Japan is prepared to take necessary measures should the Nanking Government adopt steps running counter to the developments in North China,” the Japanese official was reported to have said.—Rengo.

Fu To See Yen

KWEIHUA, Nov. 28.—General
