1935年12月28日。晨间译文。

吴铁城市长致学生的公开信。

随着全体请愿学生昨晚归来，吴铁城市长发布如下致学生的公开信：-
“经政府和地方教育当局的恳切劝告，试图前往南京递交请愿书的本地全体学生，于昨日下午三时从无锡返回上海。对于你们的归来，我不禁感到欣喜。
“当你们聚集在上海北站并占据列车以图递交请愿书时，可曾考虑到当时上海弥漫的不良气氛？公众同情你们的爱国热情，但鉴于中国目前面临的困难以及上海错综复杂的状况，反动分子企图利用局势制造骚乱。在你们聚集北站的次日，约有四千人集结，同时出现了反动的传单。一千人聚集在宝山路旁，准备闹事，企图酿成惨案。鉴于局势艰难，我尽力劝说部分学生返回学校，同时为了你们的安全起见，我被迫命令列车驶离车站。
“在你们向西出发后，我立即派遣负责官员前来照顾你们，同时请求各校校长协助劝说。我一整天都在为你们的状况担忧。幸运的是，同济大学的学生于12月25日返回，而全体学生于昨日下午归来。虽然你们的列车未抵达南京，但你们的意愿已由我转达，并已获得国民政府的接纳。既然你们已经回来，今后必须克制自己，等待能为政府提供实际服务的时机。
“关于当今青年如何报国，我在12月21日的声明中已向你们解释，无需赘述。如果我们切实且深刻地理解目前的国家困难，就会认识到，以真正的精神报国不仅仅是一时的愤慨，而是一场永恒的斗争。我们不应被情绪所误导，也不应将表象误认为实质。在过去的救国运动中，始终存在一个非常令人痛心的因素，那就是精力的滥用。这对于缓解国家危机没有任何价值，只会对社会造成伤害。真正爱国者对此深感惋惜。只有当觉醒的青年认识到国家危机的真正原因，集中精力集体报国，并在中央政府的领导下为民族的生存而奋斗时，中国才能成为一个强国。唯有如此，才可能为我们民族带回永恒的荣耀。
“希望你们能 heed 我的观点。”

pages.en:
December 28, 1935. Morning Translation.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers (Nanking
Telegram) :-

AGITATION AGAINST THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA
Precautionary Measures enforced in Nanking, Shanghai and
Hankow

Generals Koh Ching Lung, Wu Teh Chen and Chen Chi Zung
appointed as Officers-in-Charge

Precautionary measures were enforced
in Nanking as from December 26. General Koh Ching Lung
(谷正倫) has issued a proclamation containing the
following rules governing the measures:-
(1) All meetings, associations,
newspapers, magazines, publications, posters, slogans, etc.
will be suppressed when found to endanger the peace.
(2) All mail letters and telegrams
will be censored and, if necessary, will be detained
or confiscated.
(3) All steamers, vehicles and airplanes,
leaving or entering, will be inspected and, if necessary,
their operations will be prevented or their principal
routes and air lines will be obstructed.
(4) All suspicious passengers will be
searched.
(5) All suspicious organizations will
be inspected, but no intentional harm will be done.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

Students returned Shanghai Yesterday as a Result of
repeated persuasion by the Authorities

Over 1,000 students of Futan University
and various other local middle schools who left Shanghai
on December 24 for the purpose of submitting appeals to
the Nanking Authorities arrived at Kao Jao, West of
Wusih, on December 26. They could not proceed any
further because the rails there had been removed.
On the morning of December 27, Koh
Ching Lung, Nanking Gendarmerie Commander, Mr. Pan Kung
Tsai, Commissioner of the Shanghai Bureau of Education,
Mr. Li Dah Chao, a departmental chief of the Shanghai
City Government, and delegates from the Ministry of
Education and the principals and professors of the various
local schools arrived at the place and advised the students
on the trains to alight from the locomotives and to gather
at the Chung Nan Theatre, near the Wusih Station. They
then earnestly advised the students to return Shanghai
which the latter agreed to do. The students, therefore,
boarded the trains and left Wusih at 3 p.m. yesterday
and arrived at Nantziang at 6.05 p.m. when they were
conveyed to their respective schools by the vehicles
of the Shanghai City Government.
On their way to Shanghai, the students
held a conference in the trains at the which the following
decisions were reached:-
pages.zh:
1935年12月28日。晨间译件。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸（《南京电报》）：

反对华北自治运动
南京、上海和汉口实施预防措施

任命葛敬龙、吴德桢和陈其采将军为负责人

自12月26日起，南京实施预防措施。葛敬龙将军（谷正倫）发布告示，包含以下管理这些措施的规则：
(1) 凡被认为危及和平的所有集会、社团、报纸、杂志、出版物、海报、标语等，均予取缔。
(2) 所有邮件和电报均受检查，如有必要，将予以扣留或没收。
(3) 所有进出之轮船、车辆和飞机均受检查，如有必要，将阻止其运行或阻断其主要路线和航线。
(4) 所有可疑乘客均受搜查。
(5) 所有可疑组织均受检查，但不会故意造成伤害。

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

经当局反复劝告，学生昨日返回上海

复旦大学及本地各中学的一千多名学生于12月24日离开上海，旨在向南京当局递交请愿书，他们于12月26日抵达无锡西部的高桥。由于那里的铁轨已被拆除，他们无法继续前进。
12月27日上午，南京宪兵司令葛敬龙、上海市教育局局长潘公展先生、上海市政府某处处长李大钊先生，以及教育部代表和本地各学校校长、教授抵达该地，劝告列车上的学生从火车头下来，聚集在无锡车站附近的中南大戏院。随后，他们恳切劝告学生返回上海，学生们表示同意。因此，学生们登上列车，于昨日下午3时离开无锡，并于下午6时05分抵达南翔，随后由上海市政府的车辆将他们送往各自学校。
在前往上海的途中，学生们在列车上举行会议，达成以下决定：

December 28, 1935.                                  Morning Translation.

1) That the Hopei-Chahar Political Council should be
   abolished.
2) That protection should be rendered to the students
   movement.
3) That the Peiping students who were arrested should be
   released.
4) That compensation be accorded to the injured students
   in Peiping and Shanghai as well as to the relatives of
   those who have succumbed to their wounds.
5) That punishment be meted out to those responsible
   officers.
6) That all traitors be eradicated.
7) That the lost territory be recovered and that an
   expeditionary force be despatched to punish the traitor
   Yin Ju Keng.
8) That freedom of speech be accorded.

Students of the Institut Technique Franco-Chinois
to Conduct Extensive Propaganda for National
Salvation.

    In view of the critical condition of China which
is being faced with an acute national crisis, the entire
body of students of the Institut Technique Franco-Chinois
have decided to conduct an extensive propaganda for three
days commencing from to-day, with a view to arousing the
public to the necessity of national unification.

Sun Ya Middle School Students Nations' Salvation
Association to Issue Manifesto

    The Sun Ya (新亚) Middle School Students
National Salvation Association issued the following manifesto
yesterday addressed to the various government organs, public
bodies and schools throughout this country:-
    "It is indeed a great misfortune to China that
she has been subject to repeated foreign aggressions. The
wound which she received as a result of the outbreak of
the North-East Incident is extensive and serious. However,
the traitor Yin Ju Keng, taking advantage of the national
crisis, openly revolted against the National Government.
All those who have any enthusiasm at all are extremely
indignant at his activities. Our government, being
responsible for the maintenance of peace, and the prevention
of foreign aggression cannot shift its responsibility
onto others' shoulders. It should issue an official
decree to punish the traitor Yin Ju Keng with a view
to enforcing its discipline, so as to bring about the
unification of a revolutionary spirit. Under the
principle of "loving the nation whilst studying," the
students of this institut have sworn to adopt unanimous
activities with the other youths of this country, in order
to back up our government."
pages.zh:
1935年12月28日。                                  晨间译件。

1) 撤销冀察政务委员会。
2) 保护学生运动。
3) 释放被捕的北平学生。
4) 对北平和上海受伤的学生以及因伤身亡者的家属给予赔偿。
5) 惩处有关责任官员。
6) 铲除所有汉奸。
7) 收复失地，并派遣远征军惩办汉奸殷汝耕。
8) 赋予言论自由。

中法工业专门学校学生开展广泛的救国宣传。

    鉴于中国面临严重的民族危机，局势危急，中法工业专门学校全体学生决定从今天起开展为期三天的广泛宣传活动，以唤起公众对国家统一必要性的认识。

新亚中学学生救国会发表宣言

    新亚中学学生救国会昨日向全国各政府机关、公共团体和学校发表了以下宣言：
    “中国屡遭外国侵略，实乃一大不幸。因‘九一八’事变爆发而受到的创伤广泛且严重。然而，汉奸殷汝耕利用国家危机，公然反抗国民政府。凡有热血者，对其行径无不极度愤慨。我国政府负有维护和平、防止外国侵略之责，不可将此责任推卸给他人。应发布正式命令，惩办汉奸殷汝耕，以整肃纪律，从而促成革命精神的统一。本着‘读书爱国’的原则，本校学生誓与全国青年采取一致行动，以支持我国政府。”

LOCAL REPERCUSSIONS AGAINST AUTONOMY MOVEMENT
IN NORTH CHINA
- Student Activities
The train carrying 1,100 students which left Shanghai
North Station at about 5 p.m. December 24, ostensibly for
Nanking, came back on December 27, 1935. It arrived at
Nanziang at 6.25 p.m. The coaches containing the students
stopped there and the locomotive was disconnected and sent
to Markham Road Junction. On seeing the locomotive depart,
the students fearing that they would be kept at Nanziang
for the night raised a protest and began to break up the
furniture and fittings of the coaches. On being assured
by Mr. Li Dah-chao (      ), Chief of the 1st Department
of the Shanghai City Government, and several officers of
the Peace Preservation Corps, who came to the scene that
arrangements had been made to convey them to Shanghai in
buses and trucks, they became peaceful and desisted from
doing further damage. After a wait at Nanziang lasting
about an hour, twenty six motor buses were made available
for the transportation of the students. About 950 of them
boarded these vehicles, and proceeded to their respective
schools. The remaining 200, who were all students of the
Fuh Tan University, Kiangwan, were taken by train to
Kiangwan where they arrived at 10.15 p.m. The Fuh Tan

December 25, 1935. Morning Translation.

NICHI-NICHI

JAPANESE AUTHORITIES REQUEST THE S.M.C. TO EXERCISE
STRICT CONTROL OVER THE STUDENTS MOVEMENT

With the development of the students'
demonstrations against the autonomous movement in North
China, anti-Japanese activities are being openly carried
out in the Settlement, thereby arousing more uneasiness.
Mr. Ishii, Japanese Consul-General, called
on Mr. Fessenden, Secretary-General of the S.M.C., on the
morning of December 24 and requested him to exercise strict
measures. Mr. Fessenden promised to comply with the request.
The Consul-General had intended to interview
Mayor Wu but owing to pressure of work Mayor Wu was unable
personally to meet the Consul-General. Therefore, Mr. Ishii
spoke with the Mayor over the telephone and requested him
to control the movement. The Mayor promised to comply with
the request.

MAINICHI
ANTI-JAPANESE HANDBILLS PRINTED BY THE COMMERCIAL PRESS

Amongst the handbills disseminated at the
North Station and on Nanking Road, Honan Road, and other
places several anti-Japanese pamphlets were found. These
handbills were printed at the Commercial Press by several
tens of printers under the direction of one Chow Chao Chi,
an employee of the concern. 周肇基
On December 24, workmen of a certain factory
went on strike and marched to the North Station to take part
in the students' demonstration.
The Public Safety Bureau has not yet decided
what attitude to adopt towards the movement which is
assuming a serious aspect.

JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE PROTECT JAPANESE RESIDENCES

Following the demonstration held on Nanking
Road yesterday, members of the 2nd Section of the local
Japanese Consular Police immediately proceeded to the scene
and adopted precautionary measures at Japanese business
concerns and residences on this road.

December 27, 1935.
Afternoon Translation.

The Mass Livelihood(大众生活), a weekly periodical, published
the following article on December 21 :-

ARE PEIPING AND TIENTSIN STILL UNDER CHINA'S JURISLICTION?

I think the Chinese masses living outside
Peiping and Tientsin will regard me as a madman for asking
such a question: "Are Peiping and Tientsin still under
China's jurisdiction?"
To-day, military aeroplanes that are not of
Chinese ownership are daily flying over Peiping and Tientsin,
and in the latter district a large military aerodrome,
occupying a piece of land measuring about 1,000 mow, is
under construction. As I have not been to foreign countries,
I cannot say whether the flying of Chinese military aeroplanes
in Great Britain, America or Japan would be permitted. My
common sense tells me that if Peiping and Tientsin are still
Chinese territory, China should not allow such activities.
Reports have been constantly appearing in the
newspapers that the government of a "friendly nation", in
order to protect the safety of North China, is opposed to
the troops of the Chinese Government proceeding to the North
because of a certain treaty. At present, large numbers of
soldiers of the "friendly nation" have concentrated in Peiping
and Tientsin.
I personally witnessed the autonomous movement
in Tientsin. On a certain morning I saw 10 trucks, carrying
a large number of ragged drug addicts, some in military
uniforms, appear on a thoroughfare in a certain Concession
of Tientsin. I at first thought that these drug addicts
were under arrest. Two hours later rumours were prevalent
and "extras" were on sale. I bought a copy and on reading it
I learnt that these drug addicts were dare-to-die represen-
tatives who were on their way to the City Government to
demand autonomy and ready to take over the administration.
Such a state of affairs exists not only in
Peiping and Tientsin, but also in the demilitarized zones in
East Hopei which are at present forcibly occupied by the
rebel Yin Zu Keng and which have openly seceded from Nanking.
Of late, groups of "xx" soldiers, fully armed, could be seen
everyday visiting various Hsiens throughout the province of
Hopei, conducting surveys everywhere. These soldiers even
force the inhabitants to sign pro-autonomy manifestoes which
they carry with them already prepared, and those who refuse
to comply with their order are instantly shot to death.
Some time ago, our government officials
declared that no loss of China's sovereign rights would
be tolerated and that they would not yield. But do not
the present conditions in Hopei constitute loss of sovereign
rights to China? Do not the changes that have taken
place in North China indicate that the moment has come for
sacrifices?

周刊《大众生活》（The Mass Livelihood）于12月21日发表了以下文章：-

北平和天津仍在中国管辖之下吗？

我想，居住在北平和天津以外的中国民众会认为我问出这样一个问题是疯子：“北平和天津仍在中国管辖之下吗？”
今天，非中国所有的军用飞机每天都在北平和天津上空飞行，而在后者地区，一个占地约1000亩的大型军用机场正在建设中。由于我未曾出国，我无法说在英国、美国或日本是否允许中国军用飞机飞行。我的常识告诉我，如果北平和天津仍是中国领土，中国就不应允许此类活动。
报纸上不断有报道称，一个“友好国家”的政府为了保护华北的安全，因某项条约而反对中国政府军队北上。目前，大量“友好国家”的士兵集中在北平和天津。
我亲眼目睹了天津的自治运动。某天早晨，我看到10辆卡车，载着大量衣衫褴褛的吸毒者，其中一些人身穿军装，出现在天津某租界的一条主干道上。我起初以为这些吸毒者是被逮捕的。两小时后，谣言四起，“号外”开始发售。我买了一份，阅读后得知，这些吸毒者是敢死队代表，正前往市政府要求自治，并准备接管行政权。
这种情况不仅存在于北平和天津，也存在于冀东非军事区，该地区目前被叛军殷汝耕（Yin Zu Keng）强行占领，并已公开脱离南京政府。最近，每天都可以看到全副武装的“xx”士兵团体走访河北省各县，到处进行调查。这些士兵甚至强迫居民签署他们预先准备好的拥护自治的宣言，那些拒绝服从命令的人会被立即枪决。
不久前，我国政府官员声明，绝不容忍中国主权的丧失，也不会屈服。但是，河北目前的状况难道不构成对中国主权的丧失吗？华北发生的变故难道不表明牺牲的时刻已经到来吗？

December 24, 1935.    2    Afternoon Translation.

The China Sketch (中國 sketch ), Volume 5, published the
following article :- (Abbreviated Translation)

THE NORTH CHINA QUESTION

The Chinese people are paying close
attention to the autonomous movement in North China and
the activities of the shameless traitor Yin Ju Keng.
It is known to all who is at the back of these activities.
It is said that as soon as the North China Question
has been settled, China will have no other vital problems
to be solved. Such a statement will obscure public
understanding of this important question in which the
life or death of the Chinese race is bound up. We warn
the Chinese people that our most vital problem to-day
is the preservation of the Chinese race.
In the beginning the North-Eastern
Question appeared to have no connection with other parts
of China. When China's North-Eastern territory was
lost, it seemed that the affair was closed. It was not
believed at the time that the loss of the North-East
was the commencement of the collapse of the whole
of China, and would eventually develop into a problem
affecting the very existence of the Chinese race. Facts
have now proved that this belief was absolutely wrong.
We are strongly opposed to the
autonomous government instigated by the enemy. If this
movement can be suppressed temporarily, could it be
said to have settled the North China Question? Even
if there had been no movement for self-government, could
any piece of territory in which Chinese troops are not
allowed free movement, and Chinese officials and civilians
can be arrested at will, be regarded as a part of China?
There are many methods of aggression, such as by
economic rapprochement, cultural co-operation, etc.
We should not allow ourselves to be deceived but we
should pay careful attention to the fact that even a
settlement of the dispute would not give practical
benefits, but would on the contrary give rise to endless
trouble.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking Telegram) :-

MEASURES GOVERNING BAIL, ETC.

The Ministry of Justice has drawn up
the following measures governing the placing of defendants
under bail, etc.:-
During the trial of a case when it is
believed that the defendant will file an appeal which
cannot be concluded within the specified period after the
conclusion of the case, the Court may suspend the detention
of the defendant and instruct him to provide bail, or
place him under the protection and control of another person,
or restrict his place of residence. If the defendant has
already provided bail, restrictions may be placed on his
place of residence; and if restrictions have already been
placed on his residence, he may be placed under the protection
and control of another. The Judge of the Court of First
Instance, who hears the case, will personally verify whether
or not the person or shop providing the bail is acceptable, or
whether the person under whose protection and control a
defendant is placed. is in a position to fulfil his obligations

《中国素描》（The China Sketch），第5卷，发表了以下文章：-（节译）

华北问题

中国人民正密切关注华北的自治运动以及无耻汉奸殷汝耕（Yin Ju Keng）的活动。众所周知，这些活动的幕后黑手是谁。据说，一旦华北问题得到解决，中国将没有其他亟待解决的重大问题。这种说法会模糊公众对这一关乎中华民族生死存亡的重要问题的理解。我们警告中国人民，我们今天最 vital 的问题是保存中华民族。
起初，东北问题似乎与中国其他地区没有关联。当中国东北领土沦丧时，事情似乎就此终结。当时人们并不相信东北的沦丧是整个中国崩溃的开始，并最终会发展成影响中华民族生存的问题。事实现已证明，这种信念是完全错误的。
我们强烈反对由敌人煽动的自治政府。如果这一运动能被暂时镇压，能否说华北问题已得到解决？即使没有自治运动，任何不允许中国军队自由行动、中国官员和平民可被随意逮捕的领土，能被视为中国的一部分吗？
侵略的方式有很多，如经济亲善、文化合作等。我们不应让自己受欺骗，而应仔细注意这样一个事实：即使是争端的解决也不会带来实际利益，反而会引起无尽的麻烦。

关于保释等措施的规定

司法部制定了以下关于被告保释等措施的规定：-
在案件审理期间，如果认为被告将在案件结案后的规定期限内提出无法审结的上诉，法院可以暂停拘留被告，并指令其提供保释金，或将其置于另一人的保护和监管之下，或限制其居住地。如果被告已提供保释金，可以对其居住地施加限制；如果已对其居住地施加限制，可以将其置于另一人的保护和监管之下。审理该案的一审法院法官将亲自核实提供保释的个人或商号是否可接受，或者负责保护和监管被告的人是否有能力履行其义务

S. B. REGISTRY.
No D 7108.
Date 24/ 12. 1935

December 24, 1935. Afternoon translation.

Kuo Sin Weekly (国讯) published the following comment on
December 21:-

THE STUDENTS PATRIOTIC MOVEMENT

The students movement which has been quiet for
a long time is being revived. Although the movement
cannot remedy the situation in North China, it shows
that the spirit of the Chinese people is still active.
We are in full sympathy with the students.

During the past four years, the advance of the
aggressive policy of our strong neighbour has been
unprecedented. China has made concessions again and
again and our enemy is pushing on its invasion ceaselessly.

Will China be in a position to endure such
invasions for four more years?

The people should unite and work for national
salvation in order to console the students.
pages.zh:

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部登记处。
编号 D 7108。
日期 1935年12月24日

1935年12月24日。下午译件。

《国讯》周刊（Kuo Sin Weekly）于12月21日发表了以下评论：-

学生爱国运动

沉寂已久的学生运动正在复兴。虽然该运动无法补救华北的局势，但它表明中国人民的精神依然活跃。我们完全同情学生。

在过去四年里，我们强大邻国的侵略政策推进程度前所未有。中国一再让步，而我们的敌人则在不停地推进其入侵。

中国还能再忍受这样的入侵四年吗？

民众应当团结起来，为救国而努力，以慰藉学生。

pages.en:
December 24, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

NANCHI

ATTEMPTED SUICIDE OF A JAPANESE

A Japanese named Tokuichi Sakai, aged 58,
of Nagasaki arrived in Shanghai on December 21, and stayed
at the Yamato Hotel. On December 22 he removed to No. 23
Nanking Road, the home of Mr. K. Yamanaka. At about 11 p.m.
December 22, Sakai left the house saying that he had some
engagement. At 1 a.m. December 23, the local Japanese
Consular Police received a report from the Purser of the
S.S. "Kazan Maru" that he had saved a Japanese who had
attempted to commit suicide. Sakai was taken to the
Consulate, where it was revealed that he had jumped into
the river to commit suicide but was picked up by the crew
of a launch and then removed to the "Kazan Maru". Mr.
Yamanaka was ordered to appear before the Consular Police.
It is believed that Sakai is mentally deranged.

NIPPO

THE CHINESE STUDENTS MOVEMENT

The Chinese students movement has been
intensified. A characteristic of the present movement
is that the students of mission schools maintained by
British and Americans, especially those of the latter,
are taking a prominent part. This is a reflection of the
British and American attitude towards autonomy of North
China. As professors of universities seem to be instigating
the movement, developments are being carefully watched.
It is a fact that politicians who had failed to secure
office in the newly organized Chinese Government are
encouraging the movement behind the scenes.
As it is feared that these activities
may develop into an anti-Government and anti-Chiang Kai Shek
movement, the Nanking Government will adopt suppressive
measures.

The anti-autonomous movement of the
students which has spread throughout China is being
regarded by the Nanking Government as a patriotic movement,
therefore the Chinese Authorities are not suppressing it.
Recent developments indicate that the movement is being
secretly instigated from behind by third parties and
radical elements and communists. It has, therefore, been
decided to summon to Nanking the Presidents of universities
at various places and to give them instructions regarding
the policy to be adopted in directing the students.
Representatives of students will also
be summoned to Nanking before January 15 next year when
General Chiang Kai Shek will personally warn them not to
act thoughtlessly.

1935年12月24日。下午译件。

《南池》（NANCHI，音译）

一名日本人企图自杀

一名名叫酒井德一（Tokuichi Sakai）、58岁、来自长崎的日本人于12月21日抵达上海，住在大和旅馆。12月22日，他搬至南京路23号山中（K. Yamanaka）先生家中。12月22日晚11点左右，酒井离开住所，称有约会。12月23日凌晨1点，当地日本领事警察收到“加山丸”号（S.S. "Kazan Maru"）事务长的报告，称其救起了一名企图自杀的日本人。酒井被带往领事馆，据透露，他跳河自杀，但被一艘舢板的船员救起，随后被转移到“加山丸”号上。山中先生被责令向领事警察报到。据信酒井精神失常。

《日报》（NIPPO）

中国学生运动

中国学生运动正在加剧。当前运动的一个特点是，由英美人士维持的教会学校的学生，尤其是后者学校的学生，正发挥着突出作用。这反映了英美对华北自治的态度。由于大学教授似乎在煽动该运动，各方正密切关注事态发展。事实上，那些未能在 newly organized 中国政府中获得职位的政治家正在幕后鼓励该运动。
由于担心这些活动可能发展成为反政府和反蒋介石运动，南京政府将采取镇压措施。

席卷全国的学生反自治运动被南京政府视为爱国运动，因此中国当局并未对其进行镇压。最近的事态发展表明，该运动正由第三方、激进分子和共产党人在幕后秘密煽动。因此，已决定召集各地大学校长前往南京，并就指导学生所应采取的政策向他们发出指示。学生代表也将被召至南京，明年1月15日前，蒋介石将军将亲自告诫他们不要轻举妄动。

SECRET - NOT FOR PRESS PUBLICATION
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
SPECIAL BRANCH    December 24, 1935.
INTELLIGENCE REPORT
Political
LOCAL REPERCUSSIONS AGAINST AUTONOMY MOVEMENT
IN NORTH CHINA
- Activities of students
As a result of a decision reached at a meeting held
in the Fuh Tan University, Kiangwan, at 10 a.m. December 23,
about 500 students of this institution at 11 a.m. the same
day marched from Kiangwan to the North Railway Station and
demanded free rail transportation to Nanking in order that
they might impress upon the Government the necessity for
action in connection with the Autonomy Movement in North
China. With a view to frustrating their intentions, the
Public Safety Bureau placed about sixty men on East Ti Yoeh
Wei Road, Kiangwan, and erected barbed wire barricades at a
point on that thoroughfare near the Shanghai Dairy Farm.
The students, however, succeeded in evading these precautions.
On reaching the railway crossing on Paoshan Road,
the students were again hindered by the Chinese Police who
closed the railway gates, but also without effect. The
students reached the North Station at 12.50 p.m. They
demanded free transportation to Nanking and on being refused
by the Station Master boarded the coaches of a train due to
leave for Nanking at 1.20 p.m. The Railway Authorities
retaliated by moving the engine of this train out of the
Station, and later on in the day closed the booking offices
and cancelled the dispatch of all trains.
At 3.50 p.m. a warning to all persons other than the
railway staff to leave the station precincts was broadcast
on the premises of the Shanghai North Station by means of
pages.zh:

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部    1935年12月24日。
情报报告
政治类
针对华北自治运动的地方反响
- 学生活动
由于12月23日上午10时在江湾复旦大学举行的一次会议上作出的决定，该校约500名学生于当日上午11时从江湾游行至北站，要求提供免费铁路交通前往南京，以便向政府强调就华北自治运动采取行动的必要性。为了挫败他们的意图，公安局在江湾东体育会路部署了约六十名人员，并在该干道靠近上海牛奶公司的一处地点设置了铁丝网路障。然而，学生们成功避开了这些预防措施。
当到达宝山路的铁路道口时，学生们再次受到关闭铁路闸门的中国警察的阻碍，但也未奏效。学生们于下午12时50分抵达北站。他们要求免费前往南京的交通，在遭到站长拒绝后，登上了定于下午1时20分开往南京的列车车厢。铁路当局对此采取报复措施，将该列车的机车移出车站，并于当天晚些时候关闭售票处，取消所有列车的发车。
下午3时50分，通过扩音器在上海北站区域内向除铁路员工以外的所有人广播警告，要求离开车站区域。

the instruction immediately under pain of expulsion by force.
The warning was, however, ignored by the students and no
attempt was made to give effect to the threat.

At 4 p.m. December 23, 500 members of the Public
Safety Bureau and 200 members of the Peace Preservation
Corps were dispatched to the North Station with the intention
of ejecting the students from the railway coaches, but this
order was cancelled as a result, it is reported, of

The train from Hangchow, which normally arrives at

Shanghai North/at 4.05 p.m. was diverted to the Shanghai
South Station on December 23.

At about 7 p.m. General Tsai Ching-chun, Commissioner
of the Bureau of Public Safety and Mr. Pan Kung-chai, Chief
of the Bureau of Education, arrived at the Shanghai North
Station. They attempted to persuade the students to agree
to send five delegates to Nanking and the rest to return to
their school. The students, however, refused this offer.

The number of students at the North Station had
increased to about 1,600 at 9 a.m. this morning.

The Bus Service between Chapei and the Civic Centre
was suspended by official orders from 11.40 a.m. to 12.15 p.m.
on December 23, in order to render movements of students in
that area difficult.

1935年12月24日。

同时警告学生立即服从指令，否则将被强制驱逐。然而，学生们无视这一警告，当局也未试图执行这一威胁。

12月23日下午4时，500名公安局成员和200名保安队成员被派往北站，意图将学生从铁路车厢中驱离，但据报道，由于来自南京的指令，该命令被取消。

通常于下午4时05分抵达上海北站的杭州来车，于12月23日被改道至上海南站。

晚上7时许，公安局局长蔡劲军先生和教育局局长潘公展先生抵达上海北站。他们试图说服学生同意派遣五名代表前往南京，其余人返回学校。然而，学生们拒绝了这一提议。

截至今天上午9时，北站的学生人数已增至约1,600人。

为了使该地区的学生行动困难，闸北与市中心之间的公共汽车服务奉官方命令于12月23日上午11时40分至中午12时15分暂停运营。

pages.en:
December 4, 1935.
-3-
Owing to lack of locomotives, the train due to
leave Shanghai South for Hangchow at 4.40 p.m. was
cancelled and the train due to leave at 6.10 p.m. Dec. 23
did not start until 7.10 p.m.
Members of the Bureau of Public Safety are now patrolling
in motor cars along the Ziang Ying, Kiangwan and Sui Dion
Roads. These thoroughfares connect Chapei with Kiangwan
and the Civic Centre.
A large number of students gathered about 8.45 p.m.
Dec. 24 in the compound of the Continental Emporium Building,
Nanking Road, and later endeavoured to stage a demonstration
on Nanking Road. They resisted efforts by the Police to
induce them to disperse, with the result that two Police
officers were assaulted and five students arrested. The
prisoners will be brought before the Special District
Court to-day.
Efforts are being made in Chapei to induce the students
of the various schools there to assemble at the North Station
where about 1,600 have already arrived. Efforts are also
being made to induce the students of Chinese Territory south
of the French Concession to proceed to the South Station
for the purpose of commandeering locomotives to take the
train-load of students now at the North Station to Nanking.
Certain extremist elements among students of the
following local middle schools are opposing the Middle
School Students' National Salvation Federation which was
recently inaugurated on the ground that it is a subsidiary
organ of the Kuomintang :-
pages.zh:
1935年12月4日。
-3-
由于缺乏机车，原定于下午4时40分从上海南站开往杭州的列车被取消，而原定于12月23日下午6时10分发车的列车直到晚上7时10分才启动。
公安局成员目前正乘坐汽车在翔殷路、江湾路和绥定路沿线巡逻。这些道路连接闸北、江湾和市中心。
12月24日晚上8时45分左右，大量学生聚集在南京路大陆商场大楼的大院内，随后试图在南京路举行示威。他们抵制警察劝其解散的努力，导致两名警官遭到袭击，五名学生被捕。囚犯将于今日被提审至特区法院。
闸北方面正努力促使当地各校学生聚集到北站，目前已有约1,600人抵达。同时也正努力促使法租界以南华界地区的学生前往南站，目的是征用机车，将目前位于北站的一整列学生运往南京。

At about 9.30 a.m. December 22 ten representatives of the new organization assembled in the Tseng Feng Middle School, 204 Route Froeper Paris, and attempted to hold a meeting. They were prevented from doing so, however, by the school authorities who stated that no meeting could be held without permission from the French Police.

At 2 p.m. the same day, Chang Siao-tung (張小通), a representative of the local Tangpu, called at this school and informed the principal of the necessity of suppressing all illegal activities among the students.

据悉，学生中的极端分子已组织了一个名为“上海中等学校学生救国联合会”的新团体，并指派立达中学的两名学生 Chun Suh-koh (春式□) 和 Li Dah Yung (李□鏞) 负责各学校间的联络工作。

12月22日上午9时30分左右，该新组织的十名代表聚集在霞飞路204号的立达中学，试图举行会议。然而，校方阻止了他们这样做，并表示未经法国警察许可不得举行任何会议。

当天下午2时，当地党部代表张小通到访该校，告知校长有必要镇压学生中的所有非法活动。

pages.en:
December 24, 1935.

- 5 -

At 3.15 p.m. December 23, a meeting was held under
the auspices of the Middle School Students' National
Salvation Federation in the hall of the Public Recreation
Ground, 200 Dah Chih Road, Nantao. About forty persons
who claimed to represent twenty local middle schools were
present. Yang Ling ( □□ ), a student of the Fuhtan
Middle School, presided. During the meeting, representatives
of the Tseng Feng Middle School, 204 Route Prosper Paris,
and the Chung Kuo Public School, Route Sieyes, suggested
that the students of local middle schools should proceed
to Nanking for the purpose of demonstrating their opposition
to the Autonomy Movement in the North. This suggestion was
opposed by the majority of the attendance. The following
resolutions were discussed and passed :-

1. That the question regarding the appeal to the National
Government be decided later.

2. That the following sections be formed :-
(a) Secretariat
(b) General Affairs
(c) Accounting
(d) Propaganda
(e) Ticketing.

3. That a circular telegram be issued opposing the creation
of an autonomy state in the North and drawing the
attention of the Chinese public to the matter.

4. That a manifesto be issued.

5. That the National Government be requested to instruct
the Chinese Authorities at Peiping and Tientsin to
release the students recently arrested for having
participated in the demonstrations against the Autonomy
Movement.

1935年12月24日。

12月23日下午3时15分，在中学生救国联合会的主持下，在南市大直路200号的公共游乐场大厅举行了一次会议。约有四十人出席，声称代表当地二十所中学。复旦中学学生杨灵（ □□ ）担任主席。会议期间，霞飞路204号立达中学和赛爱斯路中国公学的代表建议，当地中学的学生应前往南京，以示威反对华北自治运动。这一建议遭到大多数与会者的反对。讨论并通过了以下决议：-

1. 关于向国民政府请愿的问题留待以后决定。

2. 成立以下各组：-
(a) 秘书处
(b) 总务组
(c) 会计组
(d) 宣传组
(e) 票务组。

3. 发出通电，反对在北方建立自治政权，并提请中国公众注意此事。

4. 发表宣言。

5. 请求国民政府指示北平和天津的中国当局释放近期因参加反对自治运动示威而被捕的学生。

赛爱斯路386号中国中学的学生约400人，于今天（12月24日）上午停课。

- 散发反对华北自治运动的传单

December 24, 1935.                                  Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:

AGITATION AGAINST THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA-
GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK TO SUMMON PRESIDENTS OF UNIVERSITIES

        On December 23, General Chiang Kai Shek,
President of the Executive Yuan, issued the following
order to the Ministry of Education:-
        "The situation of China has been critical
for the past years and the National Government is doing
its best in an endeavour to combat the danger.  Leaders
of the educational circles well understand the existing
situation of the nation and they should transmit their
knowledge to the people.  With a view to making people
of the educational circles become more aware of the
national position, the Ministry of Education should fix
a date on which to call a meeting at Nanking of the
principals of the colleges and higher institutions from
all the provinces and the cities under the direct
control of the Executive Yuan, where communication is
convenient, (or of deans or important teachers of colleges
and higher institutions as representatives) and of the
principals of middle schools (at most five principals
of middle schools may attend from each province or city)
so that they may learn the policies of the government
and offer their views".
        The Executive Yuan at the same time issued
another order to the Ministry of Education as follows:-
        "The government is willing to announce its
policy towards the national affairs and is particularly
willing to consider and accept the views of the youths.
Your Ministry is hereby instructed to summon one or
three students of every college or important higher
institution in all provinces and cities under the
direct control of the Executive Yuan, where communication
is convenient, to come to Nanking in company with the
principal concerned on January 15, 1936, when the
President of the Yuan will give an explanation of the
national situation and the policies of the government,
and in the meantime the students may offer their views.
Your Ministry should draw up measures relating to the
meeting".
        Yesterday the Executive Yuan issued a circular
order to the provincial governments and the city governments
in the country, instructing that the political and
military organizations should adopt guiding and peaceful
measures to deal with students, whenever they offer
their views relating to national affairs, in a manner
that neither violates their studying nor constitutes a
menace to public safety.  The order adds that any
students' movement that gets out of order should be
prohibited according to law.

Students Processions at Hankow and Other Places

        Students at Hankow, Hsuchow, Kaifeng, Anching,
Tungchow, Ningpo and other places held processions and
submitted appeals to the authorities on December 23.

蒋介石委员长将召集各大学校长

        12月23日，行政院院长蒋介石将军向教育部发布如下命令：
        “近年来中国局势危急，国民政府正竭尽全力以应对危险。教育界领袖深知国家当前局势，应将他们的知识传达给民众。为了使教育界人士更加了解国家处境，教育部应确定一个日期，在南京召集交通便利的各省及行政院直属市的高等院校校长（或由学院院长或重要教师作为代表）以及中学校长（每省或市最多可有五名中学校长参加）开会，以便他们了解政府政策并提出意见”。
        行政院同时向教育部发布了另一项命令，内容如下：
        “政府愿意公布其对国事的政策，并特别愿意考虑和接受青年的意见。兹指令你部召集行政院直属交通便利的各省及市的每一所学院或重要高等院校的一至三名学生，于1936年1月15日随同相关校长前往南京，届时院长将解释国家局势和政府政策，同时学生可提出他们的意见。你部应制定有关会议的措施”。
        昨日，行政院向全国各省市政府发布通令，指示政治和军事机构在处理学生就国事发表意见时，应采取引导和平稳的措施，既不妨碍其学业，也不构成对公共安全的威胁。该命令补充说，任何失控的学生运动均应依法予以禁止。

汉口及其他地方的学生游行

December 24, 1935. Morning Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

Futan University Students Refuse to Leave North Station

At 10.30 a.m. yesterday more than
300 students of the Futan University proceeded on foot
to the North Station from their school, proposing to
board trains to Nanking for the purpose of submitting
appeals. Li Dah Chao (李大超), Head of the First
Department of the Shanghai City Government, in conjunction
with Huang Chun Poh (黄君復), Chief of the Branch
Bureau of Public Safety at the Civic Centre, tried in
vain to dissuade them. The students reached the North
Station at 12.45 p.m. Later they all boarded the train
which was scheduled to leave the Station for Nanking
at 1.20 p.m. However, the railway authorities were
instructed not to despatch the train. Although repeated
negotiations were opened with the students, no result
was attained.

During the time when the students
were on the way to the North Station, the police of the
Bureau of Public Safety put up temporary barbed wire
barriers on Ziang Ying Road (翔殷路) and at the corner
of Paoshan and Jukong Roads. They also closed the iron
gates at Paoshan Road (Shanghai-Woosung Station) and
the gates of the North Station in the hope of obstructing
the advance of the students. However all this was of
no avail and eventually the students reached the North
Station. A large number of police and also members of
the Peace Preservation Corps were posted around the
vicinity of the North Station for the purpose of
maintaining order. They advised the students to leave
on the buses and motor cars belonging to the City Government
stationed in front of the North Station, but the students
refused to go.

At about 3.30 p.m. Dr. T.H. Lee (李登辉),
Director of the Futan University, arrived at the North
Station with Chin Tung Ying (金通尹), Chief Secretary,
and Chang Yih (张益), Head of the Registration Department
of the University, and exhorted the students to withdraw
but without avail.

From 1 p.m. yesterday till mid night,
no trains left the Station, while those which arrived
from Nanking and Hangchow were stopped at Markham Road
Station and the Shanghai South Station.

Interviewed by a reporter of this
paper yesterday, a responsible officer of the Shanghai
City Government stated that students of local universities
and middle schools had made several calls on the local
Government during the last few days to submit appeals.
The Government had already forwarded their appeals to
the Central Authorities as well as to the Peiping
Authorities. The students did not resort to demonstrations
or strikes and their movement was carried out in an orderly
manner. He added that since December 22, a majority of
the students had resumed their studies on the advice of
their principals, but a few had disregarded the instructions
of their teachers and violated the discipline of their
schools and proceeded to the North Station on December 23,
and forcibly occupied trains, thereby obstructing traffic
and endangering peace and order. Such action was most

        在学生前往北站途中，公安局警察在翔殷路（Ziang Ying Road）以及宝山路与菊恭路（Jukong Roads）转角处设置了临时铁丝网障碍。他们还关闭了宝山路（上海-吴淞站）的铁门和北站的大门，希望能阻碍学生前进。然而，这一切均无济于事，学生最终抵达北站。大量警察及保安队成员部署在北站附近以维持秩序。他们劝告学生乘坐停靠在北站前的市政府所属巴士和汽车离开，但学生拒绝离去。

December 25, 1935.    Morning Translation
(印：CRIME BRANCH)

China Times, Shun Pao and other local newspapers:

AGITATION AGAINST THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA

Trouble on Nanking Road

At 8.30 a.m. yesterday the Central Police Station in the International Settlement received secret information to the effect that a large number of students would visit Nanking to disseminate handbills and deliver open air lectures.

Fearing that the presence of these students may affect peace and order in the Settlement, a large group of detectives and policemen, led by Chinese and foreign inspectors, were detailed to patrol on Nanking Road.

Later, about 500 to 600 students and people were noticed gathering in the vicinity of the Continental Emporium near the corner of Shantung Road. The students distributed handbills. With a view to preventing incidents, the police inspectors and their subordinates peacefully persuaded the crowd to disperse, but without result. Then the Police dispersed them and some trivial trouble arose. Inspector Watson was injured in the face, Inspector Furness was hurt in the arm and face, Inspector West was injured in the face, while his helmet was damaged.

Tong Tsoong Hsiang (董崇湘), a student of Medhurst College, and Dzung Chu Wei (鄭樹慰), an exchange broker, were arrested on the spot. Order on Nanking Road was not resumed until after 11 a.m.

The two arrested persons were taken before the First Special District Court at 12.30 p.m. where they were charged with obstructing public officers in the execution of their duties (Article 135 and 136 of the Chinese Criminal Code). Inspectors Watson, Furness and West gave evidence.

After they had been interrogated by Judge Tan (戴), the two accused were sentenced to 3 months' imprisonment each, with suspension for three years. The accused were ordered to furnish shop security in case they desired to appeal.

The two accused were then taken to the Security Department of the Court. They will be set free as soon as the necessary security has been furnished.

At the time when the trouble occurred, Dzung Chu Wei was slightly injured in the head. Thus his head was bound with white cloth.

Sin Wan Pao:

Students Leave North Station

At noon December 23, some 300 students of Futan University congregated at the North Station with the intention of taking trains to Nanking to submit appeals to the authorities. Despite every persuasion by the authorities and the President of the University to induce them to return to their school, the students refused to move and remained at the Station. Furthermore, the students assaulted and injured several unarmed policemen and also distributed reactionary handbills.

《字林西报》、《申报》及其他本地报纸：

反对华北自治运动之 agitation

南京路发生骚乱

        昨日上午8时30分，公共租界中央捕房收到秘密情报，称将有大量学生前往南京散发传单并进行露天演讲。

        出于担心这些学生的出现可能会影响租界的和平与秩序，一批由中外巡官率领的侦探和警察被派往南京路巡逻。

        随后，人们注意到约有500至600名学生和民众聚集在山东路路口附近的大陆商场（Continental Emporium）一带。学生们分发传单。为了防止事态发生，警方巡官及其下属平和地劝告人群解散，但未获结果。随后警察驱散了人群，引发了一些轻微冲突。沃森（Watson）巡官面部受伤，弗内斯（Furness）巡官手臂和面部受伤，韦斯特（West）巡官面部受伤，其头盔亦受损。

        麦赫斯特学院（Medhurst College）学生董崇湘（Tong Tsoong Hsiang）和证券经纪人鄭樹慰（Dzung Chu Wei）当场被捕。南京路的秩序直到上午11点后才恢复。

        两名被捕者于下午12时30分被提审至第一特区法院，被控妨碍公务人员执行职务（《中华民国刑法》第135条和第136条）。沃森、弗内斯和韦斯特巡官出庭作证。

        经戴法官（Judge Tan）讯问后，两名被告各被判处三个月监禁，缓刑三年。被告被责令提供铺保，以备上诉之需。

        随后，两名被告被带至法院保安部。一旦提供必要的担保，他们将被释放。

        骚乱发生时，鄭樹慰头部受轻伤。因此，他的头部用白布包扎。

《新闻报》：

December 25, 1935. Morning Translation.

On the morning of December 24, a number of middle school students, instigated by elements of the Communist Party and the Social Democratic Party, gathered in the compound of the Continental Emporium Building on Nanking Road and attempted to hold a procession in the Settlement. They distributed handbills of a reactionary character. These bad elements are planning to utilize the students to disturb the peace of this locality, to obstruct communications and to create a tragedy, thereby aggravating the situation. These elements even succeeded in entering the Settlement in the hope of giving rise to an international trouble.

At 2 p.m. yesterday, the Shanghai City Government notified the Presidents of the Universities concerned to gather at the North Station to advise their students to return to school. Students of the Chih Chih and other Universities complied with the advice to return, but several hundred students of Futan University, the Tung Chi University, the Chi Kuo Middle School and the Sz Pei Middle School refused to leave the North Station. As the North Station adjoins the Settlement, it is dangerous for the students to stay at the station. Trains were then prepared and the students were removed further inland.

It is reported that the Presidents of the Universities persuaded their students to continue their studies and to elect representatives to proceed to Nanking on January 15, 1936 in compliance with the instructions of General Chiang Kai Shek.

Middle schools will comply with the order of the Ministry of Education by commencing the winter vacation at an earlier date.

Processions by Students at Nantao and Chapei

In order to support the students of Futan University, the students of the Tsin Sin (清心), the Min Lih (民立) and other middle schools at Nantao yesterday morning held processions. Starting from their respective schools, the students passed through Chung Hwa Road, Old West Gate, Fong Zia Road and South Railway Station Road, shouting patriotic slogans and distributing various kinds of handbills.

In Chapei, the students of the Ai Kuo (愛國), the Yoeh Tsin (約青) and other schools proceeded in a body along Kiangwan, Paoshan and Tatung Roads. They also passed through North Szechuan Road. Slogans were shouted and handbills distributed. The processions maintained good order and no incidents occurred.

在闸北，爱国、约青等校的学生集体沿江湾路、宝山路和大通路行进。他们还经过了北四川路。现场高呼口号并散发传单。游行秩序良好，未发生任何事件。

General Chiang Sends Telegram to Futan University
Students Urging Them to Return To School

The following telegram has been sent to the
students, c/o the Station Master of the Nanking-Shanghai
Railway by General Chiang Kai Shek, President of the

"The Government is quite willing to agree
with your views and has already instructed the Ministry

Mayor Wu to Summon the Principals of the Various
Schools

A small number of students of Futan University
forcibly occupied the North Station on the night of
December 23, thereby obstructing railway traffic and
endangering peace and order. They were advised
by the authorities to leave the station, but they refused
to go away. It is believed that their activities
are being carried out with ulterior motives. It is
reported that communists and members of the socialistic
democratic party, availing themselves of this opportunity,
are instigating the students to create disorder. In
view of this fact, Mayor Wu Teh Chen yesterday afternoon
summoned the principals of the various local universities
and instructed them to do everything possible to persuade
the students to return so as to avoid trouble.
Consequently the principals of Chiao Tung University,
Great China University, the Law College and the University

adopt all possible means to induce their students not to
proceed to Nanking but to return to their schools and

- Summary of Events at the Shanghai North Station

The students of the Fuhtan University who thronged

transportation to Nanking, remained there throughout

Parties of students from the following universities

The latter took up positions at strategic points in the

The Authorities at this time considered that the force
at their disposal was strong enough to deal with any

were informed by means of amplifiers that two trains were
being placed at their disposal, and that if they boarded
the coaches at once they would be conveyed to Nanking. The
students accepted the offer in good faith and boarded the
trains. The first of these trains left the Station at
5.05 p.m. and the second at 5.13 p.m.

It subsequently transpired that the authorities had no
intention of taking the students to Nanking. The two trains
stopped on reaching Henli, a station about thirty miles from

At 8.45 a.m. December 24, about 100 Chinese youths,

an unsuccessful attempt to persuade the workers to join them.
They then retraced their steps, and attempted to enter the
Settlement at North Honan Road. Finding the Boundary
Gate closed and the Municipal Police present in force, the
students turned eastwards along Jukong Road and adjacent
alleyways. They later filtered into the Settlement through
North Szechuen Road. A party of the Municipal Police
attempted to break up the procession at this point, and
succeeded in arresting a student of the Fuh Tan University,
Kiangwan, who assaulted a foreign member of the Force with
a bamboo pole. This prisoner will be taken before the
Special District Court on December 27. By this time the
students had succeeded in reforming into a procession, 500
strong, and they proceeded southwards along North Szechuen
Road, shouting slogans and distributing handbills.
The procession was checked by police at the Szechuen
Road Bridge and the crowd turned eastwards along North
Soochow Road. On arriving at the Chapoo Road Bridge, the
processionists again attempted to cross the Soochow Creek
southwards but were dispersed by the Police.
Twenty different kinds of propaganda literature bearing
on the autonomy movement were found in the Settlement
during the twenty-four hours ending 8 a.m., December 25.
Particulars of this literature is given in an appendix
which is attached to this report.
pages.zh:
1935年12月26日。
-4-
北站，沿宝山路前往商务印书馆印刷厂，试图说服工人加入他们，但未成功。随后他们原路返回，试图从北河南路进入租界。发现边界门关闭且工部局警察重兵把守后，学生们沿虬江路及附近小巷向东转进。后来他们通过北四川路渗入租界。一队工部局警察试图在此处驱散游行队伍，并成功逮捕了一名复旦（Fuh Tan）大学学生，该生用竹竿袭击了一名外籍警员。该囚犯将于12月27日被提解至特区法院受审。此时，学生们已成功重新集结成一支500人的游行队伍，并沿北四川路向南行进，高呼口号并分发传单。
游行队伍在四川路桥被警察拦阻，人群沿北苏州路向东转进。到达乍浦路桥时，游行参与者再次试图向南跨越苏州河，但被警察驱散。
在截至12月25日上午8时的二十四小时内，在租界内发现了二十种涉及自治运动的宣传刊物。这些刊物的详情见附于本报告后的附录。

pages.en:
December 26, 1935.
-5-
The handbills urge the people to rise up and save the
nation by opposing the Autonomy movement in North China and
the alleged ambition of the Imperialists of Japan to
obtain control over this country. Traces of communist
influence are betrayed in two handbills which purport to
emanate from the Ching Hwa University Students' National
Salvation Association ( ) and Yien King
University Students' Self Governing Society ( ),
Peiping, and the Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation
Society ( ). One of these handbills urges
that labourers and merchants should strike to support the
students. The other urges that the students movement should
be extended to embrace labourers, peasants, merchants and
soldiers.
Miscellaneous Student Activities (Dec. 24)
At 11.45 a.m. 400 students of the Dong Chi University,
Woosung, attempted to enter the Settlement via Cunningham
Road but turned back when they found the boundary gate closed.
At 9.15 a.m. December 24, 400 students of the Tsing
Sing Middle School, Loh Ka Pang Road, Nantao, left the
school and marched in processional order via Chung Hwa
and Min Kuo Roads to the City. They returned to the school
at 11.10 a.m.
Between 9 a.m. and 10.45 a.m. about 700 students of
the Great China University held a meeting in their school
on Chung San Road and decided to proceed to the Settlement
in processional order and stage a demonstration. When the
procession arrived at the school gate, another student
accused them of being communists and assaulted one of their
pages.zh:
1935年12月26日。
-5-
传单呼吁民众起来救国，反对华北的自治运动以及日本帝国主义者企图控制本国的所谓野心。有两份传单暴露出共产主义影响的痕迹，据称分别发自北平的清华大学学生救国会（ ）和燕京大学学生自治会（ ），以及上海各界救国会（ ）。其中一份传单呼吁劳工和商人罢工以支持学生。另一份则呼吁将学生运动扩展至涵盖劳工、农民、商人和士兵。
其他学生活动（12月24日）
上午11时45分，吴淞大同大学（Dong Chi University，音译，注：通常指大夏大学或类似机构，此处依音译保留或根据上下文可能指特定学校，但Dong Chi非标准拼写，暂按音译处理，若指大夏应为Great China，此处可能是OCR错误或特定小校，依指令保留原文加音译）的400名学生试图经康脑脱路（Cunningham Road）进入租界，但发现边界门关闭后折返。
12月24日上午9时15分，南市罗家浜路（Loh Ka Pang Road）清心中学（Tsing Sing Middle School）的400名学生离开学校，经中华路和民国路列队行进至市区。他们于上午11时10分返回学校。
上午9时至10时45分之间，约700名大夏大学（Great China University）学生在中山路的校内举行集会，决定列队前往租界举行示威。当游行队伍到达校门口时，另一名学生指责他们是共产党，并袭击了其中一名

pages.en:
December 26, 1935.
-6-
leaders. At this time the Chinese Police and Paotui
arrived and closed the school gate, and the students were
unable to leave.
About twenty student representatives of various classes
of the Great China University held a meeting in their school,
Chung San Road, between 2 p.m. and 3 p.m. on December 24.
They decided to reorganize the national salvation movement
in the school and formed a National Salvation Committee
of the Great China University Students' Self Control
Association.
Between 3.30 p.m. and 4.45 p.m. on December 24,
ten representatives of students of various classes of the
Kwang Hwa University held a meeting in the university at
Great Western Road (O.O.Li) and passed the following
resolutions :-
1. That the Chinese Authorities be requested to protect
the patriotic movement.
2. That open air lecturing groups be formed to function
in various villages around Shanghai in connection with
the anti-Autonomy movement.
At 6 p.m. December 24 another procession was held
by a hundred students of the Poctung Middle School in the
vicinity of Loh Ka Pang and St. Catherine's Bridge,
Nantao, and copies of a handbill bearing slogans opposing
the autonomy movement were distributed.

1935年12月26日。

领导人。此时中国警察和保甲队（Paotui）赶到并关闭了校门，学生们无法离开。
12月24日下午2时至3时之间，大夏大学各班级的约二十名学生代表在中山路的校内举行会议。他们决定重组校内的救国运动，并成立了“大夏大学学生自励会救国委员会”。
12月24日下午3时30分至4时45分之间，光华大学（Kwang Hwa University）各班级的十名学生代表在大西路（Great Western Road）的光华大学校内举行会议，并通过以下决议：
1. 请求中国当局保护爱国运动。
2. 组建露天演讲团，在上海周边各村开展反自治运动的相关活动。
12月24日下午6时，浦东中学（Poctung Middle School，音译，注：通常指浦东中学 Pudong Middle School，此处OCR可能有误，依原文音译或修正为浦东）的一百名学生又在南市罗家浜和圣凯瑟琳桥（St. Catherine's Bridge）附近举行了一次游行，并分发了印有反对自治运动口号的传单副本。

December 26, 1935.

On December 24, the following meetings of students
were held to discuss measures to be adopted in opposition
to the autonomy movement in the North :-

| Liang Zai (良才) Supplementary School, 2nd floor, Continental Building, Nanking Rd. | 68 | A presidium of five persons, including Liang Long Fang (梁龙芳), the youth responsible for the throwing of a bomb into the Yoeh Lai Dried Goods Shop, Canton Road, in October, 1934, was formed. A Liang Zai Supplementary School Students' National Salvation Association was organized. |

On December 24, telegrams were despatched by the

Government to protect the students engaged in patriotic

1935年12月26日。

学生会议

12月24日，举行了以下学生会议，讨论采取何种措施反对华北的自治运动：

12月24日，以下妇女组织发出电报，请求国民政府保护从事爱国运动的学生，并向北平学生表示同情：

pages.en:
December 26, 1935.
- 8 -
Chen Ling-yi (陳靈儀), Chairman of the Chinese Women's
League (婦女同盟會) and a committee member of the Chung
Hwa Women's Christian Temperance Association, has issued
a statement to the press to the effect that the two
organizations named have decided to withdraw from the
activities of the Shanghai Women's National Salvation
Federation which was organized at a meeting in the Chinese
Y.M.C.A. building, 599 Szechuen Road, on December 21.
Proclamation issued by Chinese Authorities
The following is a translation of a proclamation issued
on December 24 by the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commander's
Headquarters and the Shanghai City Government :-
"Owing to the fact that the student autonomy opposition
movement is fostered by patriotic motives, the Government
has regarded it in a sympathetic manner. However, since
communist and reactionary elements have been discovered
utilizing the movement as a cloak for fostering disturbances,
which may create an opportunity for international inter-
ference, Martial Law will be enforced from to-day in
districts in Chinese controlled territory where such a
measure is considered necessary. This action is being
taken in the interests of peace and order."
The following is a brief translation of a circular
notice which was issued by the Bureau of Education of the
Shanghai City Government on the evening of December 24 :-
"Circular Notice No.39196 Character 'Chiao' (教)
"(for the attention of parents of local middle school
students and principals of these institutions)
"As middle school students are young and not well
versed in the ways of life, a number of them were recently

1935年12月26日。
- 8 -
中华妇女同盟主席陈灵仪（Chen Ling-yi）兼中华基督教妇女戒酒联合会委员发表声明称，上述两个组织决定退出于12月21日在四川路599号中华基督教青年会大楼举行的会议上成立的上海妇女救国联合会的活动。
中国当局发布的公告
以下是吴淞上海卫戍司令部与上海市政府于12月24日发布的公告译文：
“鉴于学生反对自治运动是出于爱国动机，政府对此持同情态度。然而，由于发现共产党和反动分子利用该运动作为掩护来制造骚乱，这可能为国际干涉创造机会，因此在华界地区认为有必要实施戒严令的地方，将从今日起实行戒严。此举旨在维护和平与秩序。”
以下是上海市政府教育局于12月24日晚发布的通令摘要译文：
“通令第39196号‘教’字
（致本地中学生家长及各校校长）
“由于中学生年幼且不谙世事，近期有部分学生

- 9 -
instigated or compelled by evil elements to create
disturbances. An order has now been received from the
Shanghai City Government instructing that all local
public or private middle schools should close for the new
year holidays from this date, and that the principals notify
the parents of the students of these schools to keep
their children at home. Presidents of local public or
private colleges and universities are also ordered to
keep their schools closed, if circumstances warrant such
action.

Pan Kung-chai
Commissioner of the Bureau of
Education."

- Students' activities
Four hundred students of the Kiaotung University, Avenue
Haig, O.O.L. held a procession in Nantao on Dec. 25. The
procession left the school at 9 a.m. and proceeded to Chinese
territory via Route de Zikawei. Throughout the morning, they
paraded various thoroughfares in Nantao, and distributed
copies of a handbill bearing on the anti-autonomy movement.
They returned to the University about 2 p.m.
Groups of students of the Utopia University delivered
open air lectures denouncing the autonomy movement in Nantao
and the Chinese City, between 9 a.m. and 3.30 p.m. Dec. 25.
Slogans such as "Oppose the autonomy movement in the North"
and "Down with imperialists" were shouted and handbills of
three different kinds distributed. The handbills purported
to emanate from the Utopia University.

1935年12月26日。

被不良分子煽动或强迫制造骚乱。现接上海市政府命令，指示本地所有公立或私立中学自即日起放新年假，各校校长需通知学生家长将子女留在家中。本地公立或私立大专院校校长亦被命令，若情况需要，应保持学校关闭。

教育局局长
潘公展”

- 学生活动
12月25日，海格路（Avenue Haig）交通大学（Kiaotung University，注：此处英文Kiaotung通常指交通，但交大通常为Chiao Tung，此处依原文译作交通大学或保留音译，考虑到历史背景，海格路附近确有大同、交大等校，Kiaotung极可能是Jiao Tong的误拼，译为交通大学）的400名学生在南市举行游行。游行队伍于上午9时离开学校，经徐家汇路（Route de Zikawei）前往华界。整个上午，他们在南市的各条街道游行，并分发有关反自治运动的传单副本。他们于下午2时左右返回大学。
上午9时至下午3时30分之间，大同大学（Utopia University，注：Utopia即大同大学）的学生群体在南市和华界进行露天演讲，谴责自治运动。他们高呼“反对华北自治运动”和“打倒帝国主义”等口号，并分发了三种不同的传单。这些传单声称出自大同大学。

pages.en:
December 26, 1935.
- 10 -
Thirteen committee member of the Liang Zai (梁才)
Supplementary School Students' National Salvation Association
held a meeting in their school in the Continental Emporium,
Nanking Road, at 11.20 a.m. December 25. Liang Tung-fang
(      ), one of the students of the school, presided.
The following resolutions were discussed and passed :-
1. That a manifesto on the anti-autonomy movement be issued.
2. That a letter be addressed to the students at Peiping,
expressing sympathy with their patriotic movement.
3. That the National Government be requested to launch
without further delay a punitive drive against the
rebels in the North.
4. That arrangements be made to collect $0.10 from each
student to meet the expenses of the association.
5. That the request of Liang Tung-fang for permission to
resign from the post of committee member of the
association be shelved for the time being.
It will be recalled that Liang Tung-fang was arrested
by the Municipal Police on October 19, 1934, for throwing a
bomb into the Yoch Lai Dried Goods Shop, 354 Canton Road,
as a warning against dealing in Japanese products. The
missile exploded and blew off his right hand. He was
sentenced on November 17, 1934 to six months' imprisonment,
the sentence being suspended for two years.
Enquiries also show that he desires to tender his
resignation from his post in the present National Salvation
Association because his employers, the China National Goods
Company, have warned all its employees against taking part
in any political or quasi-political movement.
The Liang Zai Supplementary School operates morning
and evening classes. It has about 1,000 students on its rolls.
pages.zh:
1935年12月26日。
- 10 -
梁才补习学校学生救国会十三名委员于12月25日上午11时20分在该校（位于南京路大陆商场）举行会议。该校学生梁东方（      ）担任主席。
会议讨论并通过以下决议：
1. 发表反对自治运动的宣言。
2. 致函北平学生，对其爱国运动表示同情。
3. 请国民政府立即对北方叛乱分子发动讨伐。
4. 安排向每名学生收取0.10元，以支付本会经费。
5. 暂时搁置梁东方辞去本会委员职务的请求。
需指出的是，梁东方曾于1934年10月19日因向广东路354号裕来百货店投掷炸弹以警告勿售日货，被工部局警务处逮捕。炸弹爆炸并炸断其右手。他于1934年11月17日被判处六个月监禁，缓刑两年。
调查还显示，他之所以希望辞去目前在本救国会的职务，是因为其雇主中国国货公司已警告所有员工不得参与任何政治或类政治运动。
梁才补习学校设有早班和晚班课程。在册学生约1000人。

pages.en:
December 26, 1948.

-11-

One of the two trains carrying students which left
Shanghai North Station at about 5 p.m. Dec. 24, ostensibly
for Nanking, returned to Shanghai from Henli during the
evening of Dec. 25, passing through the North Station at
7.05 p.m. and arriving at Kiangwan at 7.15 p.m. There
were on board the train 150 students of the Engineering
College of the Dong Chi University, Kiangwan, and 150
pupils of the Medical School of the Dong Chi University,
Joosung.

The second train is still held up between Jusieh and
Jengting.

- Precautions adopted at North Railway Station by Chinese
Authorities

One hundred and fifty armed members of the Peace Preser-
vation Corps, 40 armed policemen and 40 railway policemen
carrying bamboo poles arrived at the Shanghai North Station
at about 9.30 a.m. Dec. 26, and have now taken up posts at
various points for the purpose of guarding the station.

It is reported that the precautions have been adopted
in consequence of a report that parties of students are
planning to visit the North Station some time to-day.

- Local middle schools close for New Year Holidays

All local middle schools including those in the Inter-
national Settlement and the French Concession closed for
the New Year Holidays on December 25. This action was
adopted in accordance with an order issued by the Bureau
of Education of the Shanghai City Government on the evening
of December 24 with a view to preventing middle school
students from being exploited by communist and reactionary
elements who may be endeavouring to create disturbances.
pages.zh:
1948年12月26日。

-11-

12月24日下午5时许从上海北站开出、 ostensibly（名义上）开往南京的两列载运学生的列车中，有一列于12月25日晚间从亨力（Henli，音译）返回上海，于晚上7时05分经过北站，7时15分抵达江湾。车上载有江湾大夏大学工程学院学生150名，以及兆丰（Joosung，音译）大夏大学医学院学生150名。

第二列列车仍被阻滞在居谢（Jusieh，音译）与郑亭（Jengting，音译）之间。

- 中国当局在上海北站采取的预防措施

12月26日上午9时30分左右，150名武装保安队队员、40名武装警察和40名手持竹竿的铁路警察抵达上海北站，并已在各要点布岗，以守卫车站。

据报，采取这些预防措施是因为有报告称，几批学生计划于今日某个时间前往北站。

- 本地中学因新年假期停课

包括国际租界和法租界在内的所有本地中学均于12月25日因新年假期停课。此举是根据上海市政府教育局于12月24日晚发布的一项命令采取的，旨在防止中学生被可能企图制造骚乱的共产党及反动分子利用。

pages.en:
December 26, 1935.
-13-

Local Kuomintang gives instructions to unions

Between 4.15 p.m. and 5.30 p.m. December 25, the
local Kuomintang convened a meeting of representatives of
local labour unions in its Headquarters, Feng Ling Jao, off
Route Ghisi. About 100 persons attended. Loh Ching-dz
(陸京士), a committee member of the Tangpu, gave the
following instructions :-

1) That each labour union convene a meeting for the purpose
of warning their members against allowing themselves to
be exploited by any unruly elements who are out to
embarrass the Government.

2) That the workers be told to carry on their work peacefully.

3) That the committee members of labour unions report to the
Tangpu any illegal activities or tendency towards illegal
activities on the part of labourers which may come to
their notice.

4) That the committee members should make secret investigations
regarding the activities of unruly elements and report
the results of their investigations to the Kuomintang
as soon as possible.

Anti-Japanese propaganda

During the evening of December 25 a number of handbills
of an anti-Japanese nature were found in the New World
Amusement Centre, Bubbling Well Road. The handbills appeared
to have been deliberately left in places where they they
could be easily seen by members of the public who are
frequenting the resort.
pages.zh:
1935年12月26日。
-13-

当地国民党向工会发出指示

12月25日下午4时15分至5时30分之间，当地国民党在其总部凤林角（Feng Ling Jao，音译，靠近吉司菲尔路）召集了当地各工会代表会议。约有100人出席。党部委员陆京士（Loh Ching-dz）发出如下指示：

1) 各工会召开会议，警告其会员不要让自己被任何企图使政府难堪的不法分子所利用。

2) 告知工人和平从事工作。

3) 工会委员如发现工人有任何非法活动或非法活动倾向，应向党部报告。

4) 委员应对不法分子的活动进行秘密调查，并尽快将调查结果报告给国民党。

反日宣传

12月25日晚间，在南京路新世界游乐中心发现若干反日性质的传单。这些传单似乎是被故意留在公众经常光顾该娱乐场所时容易看到的地方。

pages.en:
Brief particulars of propaganda relating to the movement

December 27, 1935.
- 7 -
Miscellaneous
Rent Reduction Federation of all Tenants in Shanghai
- removal of office
The Rent Reduction Federation of All Tenants in
Shanghai has been removed from 1342 North Szechuen Road
to its old address, 173 Chun Kai Siek Road, Chapei.
Bomb Explosion on Darroch Road.
While a Chinese hawker was proceeding along Darroch
Road about 10.45 a.m. December 26, he dropped a basket of
various articles which he was carrying on the pavement and
an explosion followed injuring the hawker and a Chinese
youth who was close at the time. The hawker was taken
to hospital where he will require three weeks treatment.
The youth was also taken to Hospital, but discharged as
his injuries were superficial. The article among the
hawker's wares which exploded was a tin canaster which
contained .32 bullets and an explosive substance. The
hawker states that he purchased the canaster from two
beggar boys whom he met on a street in Chapei.
Military
Szechuen Military Officers pass through Shanghai
Sixteen officers belonging to the 5th Brigade of the
Joint Hunan, Hupeh and Szechuen Bandit Suppression
Forces arrived in Shanghai from Hangchow on December 24.
They left for Nanking en route to Szechuen in the s.s.
"Kieng Zung" at 3.30 a.m. December 27.
pages.zh:
1935年12月27日。
- 7 -
杂项
上海全体租户减租联合会——迁址
上海全体租户减租联合会已从北四川路1342号迁回其原址闸北春凯瑟克路（Chun Kai Siek Road，音译）173号。
达罗克路炸弹爆炸事件。
12月26日上午10时45分左右，一名中国小贩沿达罗克路行走时，将随身携带的一篮杂物掉落在人行道上，随后发生爆炸，致使该小贩及当时在附近的一名中国青年受伤。小贩被送往医院，需治疗三周。该青年也被送往医院，但因伤势轻微已出院。小贩货物中发生爆炸的物品是一个听装罐，内装.32口径子弹及爆炸物。小贩称，该听装罐是从他在闸北某条街道上遇到的两名乞儿手中购买的。
军事
四川军官途经上海
湘鄂川三省剿匪联军第五旅的十六名军官于12月24日从杭州抵达上海。他们于12月27日凌晨3时30分乘坐“江顺”轮离开上海，经南京前往四川。

December 26, 1935. Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao (Evening Edition) and other local newspapers :-
AGITATION AGAINST THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA
General Chiang Kai Shek to address students by radio at
Zangchow Station

The University Students Petitioning
Groups organized by over ten local universities and middle
schools left here on several trains at 5 p.m. yesterday
and arrived at Tsingyangkong (青陽港) sometime after
6 p.m. There the authorities tried in vain to persuade
them to return home. The trains then proceeded to
Quinsan where the drivers left. One of the trains was
then driven by the students themselves and according to
information obtained from reliable sources, this
train has already reached Soochow. The students intended
to go further, but the authorities there had already
removed a part of the tracks. The students were notified
by the authorities of this fact and were obliged to
remain at Soochow Station.
The railway administration received
telegraphic instructions this morning from the Ministry
of Railways directing it to convey the students by train
to Zangchow (常州). General Chiang Kai Shek will
endeavour to persuade the students through the Central
Broadcasting Station (Wave length 660) to return to their
homes. The railway authorities have therefore installed
radio receiving sets at the Zangchow Station. The students
at Soochow will be carried to Zangchow as soon as the
tracks have been repaired.

Pan Kung Tsai tried in vain to persuade the students to
return Shanghai

According to the Central News Agency,
the students, when they arrived at Quinsam, were advised to
return to Shanghai by Pan Kung Tsai, Chief of the Shanghai
Bureau of Education, and the delegates of the Ministry
of Education, but the students would not listen to them.

Authorities still post police around the vicinity of the
North Station

The armed members of the Peace Preservation
Corps were withdrawn from the North Station at 7 p.m.
yesterday, but numbers of policemen and detectives
have been posted in the vicinity as a matter of precaution.
A party of students from the Pootung
Middle School proceeded to the North Station last night
with the intention of going to Nanking to submit appeals,
but were stopped by the police and military officers.
At about 5 p.m. yesterday two groups
of students from the Dung Chi University and the Pan Ming
(培明) Middle School for Girls were stopped by the police
at the corner of Paoshan and Boundary Roads. Over 40 students
of the Pan Ming Middle School entered the North Station,
and four of them succeeded in boarding trains. The remaining
students then joined the students of Dung Chi University
and proceeded to the Chinan University by walking along
the railway track.
pages.zh:
1935年12月26日。晨间译文。

《新闻报》（晚刊）及其他本地报纸：
反对华北自治运动的 agitation（煽动/运动）
蒋介石将军将在常州站通过广播向学生讲话

大学生请愿
由本地十余所大学和中学组织的团体于昨日下午5时乘多趟列车离开此地，并于下午6时后某时抵达青阳港。当局在那里试图劝返他们，但未成功。列车随后驶往昆山，司机下车。其中一列列车随后由学生自行驾驶，据可靠消息来源，该列车已抵达苏州。学生打算继续前行，但当地当局已拆除部分铁轨。当局将此情况通知学生，他们被迫留在苏州站。
铁路局今晨收到铁道部电令，指示用火车将学生运往常州。蒋介石将军将通过中央广播电台（波长660）努力劝说学生回家。因此，铁路当局已在常州站安装收音设备。一旦铁轨修复，苏州的学生将被运往常州。

潘公展劝学生返回上海未果

据中央通讯社报道，学生抵达昆山时，上海市教育局局长潘公展及教育部代表劝告他们返回上海，但学生不听劝阻。

当局仍在北站附近部署警察

昨晚7时，武装保安队队员从北站撤出，但作为预防措施，仍有大量警察和侦探部署在附近。
昨晚，一批浦东中学学生前往北站，意图前往南京递交请愿书，但被警察和军官拦阻。
昨天下午5时许，两批来自大夏大学和培明女中的学生在宝山路与界路转角处被警察拦阻。培明中学的40多名学生进入北站，其中四人成功登上列车。其余学生随后与大夏大学学生会合，沿铁路轨道步行前往暨南大学。

December 26, 1935. Morning Translation.

Students hold procession in Nantao districts

At about 10 a.m. yesterday, more than
20 students of the Ta Dong (大東) University, Nantao,
carrying with them a quantity of handbills, etc., held
a procession along Pon Lai Road (蓬萊路) and Chung
Hwa Road (中華路), Nantao. Over 400 students of
Chiao tung University also held a procession in Nantao.
The processions were orderly. The students passed
through the French Concession; the police did not
interfere.

The attitude of the authorities

The authorities will adopt peaceful
measures to deal with the students. Severe punishment
will be imposed on those reactionary elements who are
instigating the students to create disturbances.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking Telegram) :-

National Government orders Martial Law in Shanghai, Nanking
and Hankow

The following mandate was proclaimed
by the National Government on December 25:-
"The students movement in Peiping has
spread to other parts of the country. The patriotism
of the students is regarded with sympathy by the public,
but reactionary and bad elements are taking advantage
of the situation to create disturbances. The Garrison
Commissioners at Nanking, Shanghai and Hankow have
discovered many slogans and handbills of a reactionary
nature. Upon receipt of this information, the National
Government has instructed the above three Garrison
Commissioners to declare martial law, and has furthermore
ordered the Military Affairs Commission to instruct them
to enforce martial law within their districts with effect
from 1 a.m. December 26."

China Times and other local newspapers:

Mayor Wu and the Students Demonstrations.

At noon yesterday Mayor Wu Te Chen
entertained a number of local bankers, prominent merchants
and educationalists to a tiffin at the Shanghai City
Government. Among those present were Doo Yuet Sun, Wang
Hsiao Lai, Yue Tsao Ding and Wang Pah Chi.
During the meal, Mayor Wu gave an
explanation of the measures adopted by him in dealing with
students' demonstrations.
All those present expressed their
approval of the measures adopted by the Mayor and their
willingness to render assistance.

China Times and other local newspapers:-

THE NEW PRESIDENT OF SECOND BRANCH KIANGSU HIGH COURT

Dr. Hsu Wei Tseng, the newly appointed
President of the 2nd Branch Kiangsu High Court, took over
his new post on December 25, while the retiring President
Sun Chia Nyi, who has been transferred to the Presidency
of the Hopei High Court, will leave here for Nanking on
December 27.

1935年12月26日。晨间译件。

学生在南市地区举行游行

昨日上午10时许，南市大东大学（Ta Dong University）学生二十余人，携带大量传单等物，沿蓬萊路及中華路举行游行。交通大学亦有四百余名学生在南市举行游行。游行秩序井然。学生队伍穿过法租界，警方未加干涉。

当局的态度

当局将采取和平措施处理学生问题。对于那些煽动学生制造骚乱的反动分子，将予以严惩。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸（《南京电报》）：

国民政府下令在上海、南京和汉口实施戒严

国民政府于12月25日发布如下命令：
“北平的学生运动已蔓延至全国其他地区。学生的爱国热情得到公众的同情，但反动不良分子正利用局势制造骚乱。南京、上海和汉口的卫戍司令官发现了许多具有反动态性质的标语和传单。获悉此情况后，国民政府已指令上述三位卫戍司令官宣布戒严，并进一步命令军事委员会指示他们在各自辖区内自12月26日凌晨1时起实施戒严。”

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

吴市长与学生示威

昨日中午，吴铁城市长在上海市政府设午宴招待本地银行家、著名商人和教育家。出席者包括杜月笙、王晓籁、岳朝鼎和王柏奇。
席间，吴市长就其处理学生示威所采取的措施作了解释。
所有在场人士均对市长采取的措施表示赞同，并愿意提供协助。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

江苏高等法院第二分院新任院长

新任江苏高等法院第二分院院长徐维曾博士于12月25日到职，而卸任院长孙嘉异已调任河北高等法院院长，将于12月27日离沪赴京。

SECRET - NOT FOR PUBLICATION
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
SPECIAL BRANCH    December 27, 1935.
INTELLIGENCE REPORT
Political

LOCAL REPERCUSSIONS AGAINST AUTONOMY MOVEMENT
IN NORTH CHINA

- Student activities

During the morning of December 26, three hundred
students of the Kiangse Vocational School and the Tsing
Sing Middle School, Nantao, paraded along various streets
in the vicinity of the West Gate as a means of demonstrating
their opposition to the establishment of the autonomous state
in North China. Students at the head of the procession carried
a white cloth banner bearing a picture of students being shot
down by policemen and an inscription worded as follows :-
"The police in Peiping massacred the students."

A meeting of the Kwang Hwa University Students'
National Salvation Association was convened at 1 p.m. on
December 26 in the premises of the university on Great
Western Road. Hu Ts-ning ( 胡 庶 華 ) presided. It was
decided to cancel a proposal to send students from the
School to Nanking, and other autonomy opposition activities
pending a reply from the National Government to the demands
made by the students of Shanghai. It was decided to send
a telegram to Nanking asking that this reply be given as
soon as possible and that particulars of the future plans
of the Government be announced.

Students of the Fuh Tan University who did not take
part in the demonstration at the Shanghai North Station on
December 24, have organized a "Support Committee" for the
purpose of affording relief to their fellow students who

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别支部    1935年12月27日。
情报报告
政治类

针对华北自治运动的本地反响

- 学生活动

12月26日上午，南市江西职业学校和清心中学三百名学生，在西门附近各街道游行，以示反对在华北建立自治政权。游行队伍前列的学生举着一面白布横幅，上面印有警察枪杀学生的图片，并写有以下文字：
“北平警察屠杀学生。”

12月26日下午1时，光华大学学生救国会在大西路该校校舍内召开会议。胡庶华主持。会议决定，在国民政府对上海学生提出的要求作出答复之前，取消派遣学生前往南京及其他反对自治活动的提议。会议决定向南京发送电报，要求尽快给予答复，并公布政府未来的计划详情。

未参加12月24日在上海北站示威的复旦大学学生，组织了一个“支援委员会”，旨在援助那些

pages.en:
left Shanghai by train on December 24 to present an appeal
to the National Government. The committee consists of
fifteen members. At 3.45 p.m. Dec. 26, twelve Chinese
newspaper reporters were received by the Committee in the
Library of the Fuh Tan University and were urged to render
assistance.
At 5.45 p.m. Dec. 26, nine members of the Liang Zai
Supplementary School Students' National Salvation Association
held a meeting in their school in the Continental Emporium
Building, Nanking Road, and passed the following resolutions:-
1) That all students of the Liang Zai Supplementary School
and its branches be urged to join the movement.
2) That in view of the financial straits of the Association,
efforts be accelerated to collect contributions from
the students of the school.
In connection with the first-mentioned resolution,
copies of a notification have been prepared for distribution
among the Liang Zai students. A translation of the
notification is as follows :-
Dear Brethren,
The fate of our country is in the balance and circum-
stances will not permit us to wait for further opportunities.
We believe that only the strength of the people can save our
country. We are educated and hot-blooded youths and it is
our duty to rouse the people to fight against our enemy. It
is our duty to save the country.
We have followed the example of various universities and
middle schools and organized a branch of the Student National
Salvation Association, and now we request you students to
send representatives to participate in a joint meeting to be
held at our institution on the second floor of the Continental
Emporium.
pages.zh:
于12月24日乘火车离开上海向国民政府请愿的同学。该委员会由十五名成员组成。12月26日下午3时45分，委员会在复旦大学图书馆接待了十二名中国报社记者，并敦促他们提供协助。
12月26日下午5时45分，良宰补习学校学生救国会九名成员在南京路大陆商场大楼内的该校校舍举行会议，并通过以下决议：
1) 敦促良宰补习学校及其分校的所有学生加入该运动。
2) 鉴于本会财政困难，加快向本校学生募集捐款。
关于第一项决议，已印制通知副本分发给良宰学生。通知译文如下：
各位同胞：
国家命运危在旦夕，形势不容我们再等待其他机会。我们相信，只有人民的力量才能拯救我们的国家。我们是受过教育的热血青年，唤醒民众抗击敌人是我们的责任。拯救国家是我们的责任。
我们效仿各大学和中学的榜样，组织了学生救国会分会，现恳请贵校学生派代表参加将在大陆商场二楼我校举行的联席会议。

Heads of Fuh Tan and Chinan Universities resign their posts

It is reported that Dr. Li Tung-hui (      ),
President of the Fuh Tan University and Mr. Ho Pin-soong
(      ), President of the Chinan University have tendered
their resignations, in consequence of the way their positions
have been embarrassed by the unruly behaviour of the students
of these schools. The students of the Fuh Tan University
issued a manifesto on December 26 urging Dr. Li Tung-hui to
withdraw his resignation.

The train service on Nanking-Shanghai Railway, which
has been suspended since 1.20 p.m. December 23, was partly
resumed at 8 a.m. December 26 when a train left the Shanghai
North Station for Soochow carrying 500 passengers.

Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

AGITATION AGAINST THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA.

Martial Law Ordered In Shanghai.

Yesterday the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison
Commissioner's Headquarters issued the following proclamation:-
"A telegram from the Military Affairs
Commissioner has been received transmitting an order issued
by the National Government which states that according to
information obtained by the Garrison Commissioners at
Shanghai, Nanking and Hankow, reactionary and bad elements
are taking advantage of the students' movements to create
disturbances, and instructs the above three Garrison
Commissioners to declare martial law.
"In compliance with this order, it is hereby
notified that martial law will be declared from this date in
Shanghai."

Since the commencement of the students'
movements in Shanghai, local reactionary elements have
been making every effort to extend their activities. The
Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters
recently received information to the effect that outsiders
have gained admittance to various schools to instigate the
students. The school authorities were ordered to take
such outsiders, when discovered, to the local military and
police authorities.

A section of the group of students proceeding
to Nanking (mainly those of Tungchi University) returned to
Shanghai at 7 p.m. December 25, but the majority, who had
reached Soochow, arrived at Wusih at dawn yesterday. The
railway administration were instructed to remove the
tracks so as to stop the train occupied by the students,
but the latter repaired the tracks.
On arrival at Wusih, the authorities there
tried in vain to persuade the students to return. It is
reported that the station master of the Tseu Ching Hong
(周泾巷) has been forced to accompany the students.
The authorities in Nanking have given strict
orders to the railway administration to co-operate with the
military authorities in persuading the students not to
proceed any farther.
The Shanghai City Government has detailed Mr.
Pan Kung Tsai, Commissioner of the Education Bureau, Mr. Ma
Tsoong Yung, Secretary of the Ministry of Education, and
Dr. Lee Teng Hui, Principal of Futan University, to proceed
to Wusih to persuade the students.
According to information from various circles,
it is believed that the entire body of students may return
to their schools.

A telephone message from Wusih states that
the train occupied by the students is at a point three miles
west of Wusih. General Koh Ching Lung, Garrison Commissioner
of Nanking, arrived at Wusih and in company with the
Magistrate of Wusih, Pan Kung Tsai, Commissioner of the
Shanghai Bureau of Education, and others, personally advised
the students to return and to appoint representatives to
proceed to Nanking next month to attend an interview to be
given by General Chiang Kai Shek. The students accepted

December 27, 1935. Morning Translation.

NICHI-NICHI

A BOMB EXPLOSION ON DARROCH ROAD

At 10.45 a.m. December 26, a Chinese second-hand goods hawker named Chen Ah Pao, aged 39, residing in Chapei, bought from two young ragpickers on Darroch Road an iron tin similar in shape to a cigarette tin for which he had paid 2 coppers. On finding that the tin contained a bomb the hawker was very pleased over the bargain. He placed the tin in one of the baskets which he was carrying. On arriving in front of the Kiyo Kan Hotel on Darroch Road he placed the baskets on the ground preparatory to taking a short rest. At this moment, the bomb exploded with a terrific noise. The hawker received serious injuries to his right thigh, while a Chinese boy named Wen Yung Fah, aged 17, residing at No. 1, Dong Foh Li, Jukong Road, was injured in the left leg. Chinese constable No. 30 of the East Wang Yang Road Station arrived at the scene immediately and sent for the Chapei ambulance.
The two injured persons were removed to Poo Tien Hospital on Hsin King Road where they were given first-aid treatment. The hawker was later removed to Lester Hospital as his injuries were very serious.
Police officers from Dixwell Road arrived at the scene and made an investigation. The Japanese Naval Landing Party also despatched a number of men and adopted precautionary measures.
At about 2 p.m. officers of the Public Safety Bureau took Wen Yung Fah to the scene of the explosion and carried out a reconstruction of the incident. An official of the Public Safety Bureau stated that owing to the serious condition of the hawker he could not be questioned so as to ascertain in what manner the bomb had come into his possession.

JAPANESE NAVAL LANDING PARTY TO HOLD REHEARSAL PARADE ON DECEMBER 30

Members of the Japanese Third Fleet and the Naval Landing Party will hold a new year parade in Hongkew Park and on Kiangwan Road on January 4, commencing at 10.30 a.m. Vice-Admiral Oikawa will review the parade. 《日日新闻》

达罗克路炸弹爆炸事件

12月26日上午10时45分，一名居住在闸北、39岁的中国二手货小贩陈阿宝，在达罗克路从两名年轻拾荒者手中以两枚铜板购买了一个形状类似香烟盒的铁罐。小贩发现罐内装有炸弹后，对这桩便宜买卖感到非常高兴。他将铁罐放入随身携带的一个篮子中。当走到达罗克路的清友馆酒店（Kiyo Kan Hotel）前时，他将篮子放在地上准备稍作休息。此时，炸弹发出巨响爆炸。小贩右大腿受重伤，而居住在菊工路（Jukong Road）东福里1号、17岁的中国男孩温永发左腿受伤。东旺洋路巡捕房第30号华捕立即赶到现场，并呼叫闸北救护车。
两名伤者被送往新康路的宝田医院接受急救。由于小贩伤势严重，随后被转送至莱斯德医院。
狄思威路巡捕房的警官赶到现场进行调查。日本海军陆战队也派遣多名人员并采取预防措施。
下午2时许，公安局官员将温永发带至爆炸现场，进行了案情重现。公安局一名官员表示，由于小贩病情严重，无法对其进行讯问，以查明炸弹是如何落入其手中的。
